title.zh: 卷二百五十四 列傳第十三 侯益 張從恩 扈彥珂 薛懷讓 趙贊 李繼勳 藥元福 趙晁
title.en: Volume 254 Biographies 13: Hou Yi, Zhang Cong'en, Hu Yanke, Xue Huairang, Zhao Zan, Li Jixun, Yao Yuanfu, Zhao Chao
title.raw: 卷二百五十四 列傳第十三 侯益 張從恩 扈彥珂 薛懷讓 趙贊 李繼勳 藥元福 趙晁 Volume 254 Biographies 13: Hou Yi, Zhang Cong'en, Hu Yanke, Xue Huairang, Zhao Zan, Li Jixun, Yao Yuanfu, Zhao Chao

sentences.zh: 侯益，汾州平遙人。

translations.literal: Hou Yi was a man of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi was a native of Pingyao in Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖父以農為業。

translations.literal: His grandfather took farming as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather made his living as a farmer.

sentences.zh: 唐光化中，李克用據太原，益以拳勇隸麾下。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua era of Tang, Li Keyong held Taiyuan; Yi, by his boxing prowess and courage, was placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guanghua era of Tang, when Li Keyong held Taiyuan, Hou Yi entered his service on account of his skill in boxing and his bravery.

sentences.zh: 從莊宗攻大名，先登，擒軍校，擢為馬前直副兵馬使。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Zhuangzong in the attack on Daming, he was first to scale the wall, captured a military inspector, and was promoted to deputy commander of the Vanguard Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Zhuangzong in the assault on Daming, was the first man over the wall, captured an enemy officer, and was promoted to deputy commander of the Vanguard Guard.

sentences.zh: 征劉守光，先登，遷軍使。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Liu Shouguang, he was again first to scale the wall and was transferred to army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Liu Shouguang he again led the assault and was promoted to army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 破洺州，為機石傷足，莊宗親以藥傅其瘡。

translations.literal: When Ming Prefecture was taken, he was wounded in the foot by a catapult stone; Emperor Zhuangzong personally applied medicine to his wound.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Ming Prefecture he was struck in the foot by a catapult stone; Emperor Zhuangzong personally dressed the wound.

sentences.zh: 及愈，改護衛指揮使。

translations.literal: When he recovered, he was made commander of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After he recovered he was appointed commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 梁小將李立、李建以驍勇聞，軍中憚之。

translations.literal: The Liang junior generals Li Li and Li Jian were famed for fierce valor, and the army feared them.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang junior generals Li Li and Li Jian were renowned for their ferocity, and the army stood in awe of them.

sentences.zh: 會莊宗與梁人戰河上，益挺身出鬥，擒其二將，遷馬前直指揮使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong fought the Liang on the Yellow River, Yi stepped forward to duel, captured both generals, and was promoted to commander of the Vanguard Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong fought the Liang along the Yellow River, Hou Yi stepped forward to fight, captured both generals, and was made commander of the Vanguard Guard.

sentences.zh: 莊宗入汴，為本直副都校。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Yi was made deputy commander of the main guard unit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong entered Bian, Hou Yi was appointed deputy commander of the main guard unit.

sentences.zh: 從明宗討趙在禮於鄴。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Mingzong in the campaign against Zhao Zaili at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Mingzong in the campaign against Zhao Zaili at Ye.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍推戴明宗，益脫身歸洛，莊宗撫其背出涕。

translations.literal: When the armies acclaimed Emperor Mingzong, Yi slipped away and returned to Luoyang; Emperor Zhuangzong stroked his back and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies acclaimed Emperor Mingzong, Hou Yi made his way back to Luoyang; Emperor Zhuangzong stroked his back and wept.

sentences.zh: 明宗立，益面縛請罪，明宗曰：「爾盡忠節，又何罪也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Yi came bound to ask pardon; Emperor Mingzong said, "You fulfilled your loyalty and integrity—what crime is there?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Hou Yi came with his hands bound to ask pardon. The emperor said, "You have done your duty with loyalty and integrity—what crime have you committed?

sentences.zh: 」改本直左廂都校。

translations.literal: " He was made commander of the left wing of the main guard.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made commander of the left wing of the main guard.

sentences.zh: 天成初，朱守殷據夷門叛，益率所部斬關先入。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era, Zhu Shouyin rebelled and held Yimen; Yi led his troops, cut through the gate, and entered first.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tiancheng era, when Zhu Shouyin rebelled and seized Yimen, Hou Yi led his men through the gate in the van of the assault.

sentences.zh: 轉左右馬前從馬直都校、領潘州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to commander of the left and right vanguard horse guards and concurrently made prefect of Pan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the left and right vanguard horse guards and concurrently appointed prefect of Pan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王都據定州叛，益從王晏球攻討。

translations.literal: When Wang Du rebelled and held Ding Prefecture, Yi followed Wang Yanqiu in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Du rebelled and held Ding Prefecture, Hou Yi joined Wang Yanqiu in the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 會契丹來援，益逆擊之，破其眾唐河北，克其城，授寧州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Khitan came to their aid, Yi met them in counterattack, broke their forces in Hebei, took their city, and was appointed prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan came to their relief, he met them in a counterattack, routed their forces in Hebei, captured their city, and was appointed prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 入為羽林軍五十指揮都校、領費州刺史。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as commander of the fifty companies of the Imperial Forest Army and concurrently prefect of Fei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as commander of the fifty companies of the Imperial Forest Army and concurrently appointed prefect of Fei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時夏帥李仁福卒，子彜超擅命自立，以邀節鋮，命益帥師討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Xia commander Li Renfu died; his son Yichao seized power on his own authority to demand a military commission, and Yi was ordered to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xia commander Li Renfu died; his son Yichao seized power on his own authority to demand a military commission, and Hou Yi was ordered to lead an army against him.

sentences.zh: 明宗不豫，遽追還。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong fell ill and he was hurriedly recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong fell ill, he was hurriedly recalled.

sentences.zh: 應順初，潞王舉兵鳳翔，以益為西面行營都虞侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yingshun era, the Prince of Lu raised troops at Fengxiang; Yi was made chief adjutant of the western campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingshun era, when the Prince of Lu raised troops at Fengxiang, Hou Yi was appointed chief adjutant of the western campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 益知軍情必變，稱疾不奉詔，執政怒，出為商州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi knew the army's temper would surely shift, pleaded illness and did not obey the order; the chief ministers were angry and he was sent out as prefect of Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi knew the army's loyalty would not hold, pleaded illness and refused the order; the chief ministers were angered and he was posted out as prefect of Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蜀軍寇金州，益率鎮兵襲擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Shu forces raided Jin Prefecture; Yi led the garrison in a surprise attack and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu forces raided Jin Prefecture, he led the garrison in a surprise attack and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 詔賜襲衣、名馬，加西面行營都巡檢使。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed ceremonial robes and a famous horse, and added the post of chief inspector of the western campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted ceremonial robes and a famous horse by edict and was additionally appointed chief inspector of the western campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 晉初，召為奉國都校、領光州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, he was recalled as commander of the Fengguo Army and concurrently made military governor of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin dynasty he was recalled as commander of the Fengguo Army and concurrently appointed military governor of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 范延光反大名，張從賓據河陽為聲援。

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang rebelled at Daming; Zhang Congbin held Heyang in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang rebelled at Daming, while Zhang Congbin held Heyang to support him.

sentences.zh: 晉祖召益，謂曰：「宗社危若綴旒，卿能為朕死耶？

translations.literal: The Jin founder summoned Yi and said, "The altars of state hang by a single thread—can you die for Us?
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder summoned Hou Yi and said, "The realm hangs by a thread—will you give your life for me?

sentences.zh: 」益曰：「願假銳卒五千人，破賊必矣。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "I ask only five thousand crack troops; breaking the rebels is certain.
translations.idiomatic: " Hou Yi replied, "Give me five thousand elite troops and I shall surely break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」以益為西面行營副都部署，率禁兵數千人，次虎牢。

translations.literal: " Yi was made deputy commander-in-chief of the western campaign headquarters, led several thousand imperial troops, and encamped at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made deputy commander-in-chief of the western campaign headquarters, led several thousand imperial troops, and encamped at Hulao.

sentences.zh: 從賓軍萬餘人，夾汜水而陣。

translations.literal: Congbin's army numbered more than ten thousand and drew up its battle line along both banks of the Si River.
translations.idiomatic: Congbin's army of more than ten thousand men drew up along both banks of the Si River.

sentences.zh: 益親鼓，士乘之，大敗其眾，擊殺殆盡，汜水為之不流，從賓乘馬入水溺死。

translations.literal: Yi personally beat the drums; the men took heart from it, routed the enemy host utterly, and killed nearly all of them—the Si ceased to flow—and Congbin rode his horse into the water and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi beat the drums in person; the men took heart, routed the enemy utterly, and killed nearly all of them until the Si ran with blood; Congbin rode into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 築京觀，刻石紀功，晉祖大喜，拜河陽三城節度，充鄴都行營都虞候。

translations.literal: He built a victory mound of skulls and carved stone to record the achievement; the Jin founder was greatly pleased, appointed him military governor of the Three Cities of Heyang, and made him chief adjutant of the Ye capital campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a victory mound of enemy skulls and set up a stone monument to record his achievement. The Jin founder was overjoyed, appointed him military governor of the Three Cities of Heyang, and made him chief adjutant of the Ye capital campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 會延光以城降，移鎮潞州。

translations.literal: When Yanguang surrendered the city, Yi was transferred to govern Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang surrendered the city, Hou Yi was transferred to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天福四年，晉祖追念虎牢之功，遷武寧軍節度、同平章事，遣中使謂益曰：「朕思卿前年七月九日大立戰功，故復以此月此日徙卿鎮彭門，領相印。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianfu, the Jin founder recalled the achievement at Hulao, transferred him to military governor of the Wuning Army with the title of co-equal chief minister, and sent a palace envoy to tell Yi, "We recall your great battle achievement on the ninth day of the seventh month two years ago, and therefore on this month and this day move you to govern Peng Gate and grant the seal of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianfu the Jin founder recalled his victory at Hulao, transferred him to military governor of the Wuning Army with the title of co-equal chief minister, and sent a palace envoy to say, "I remember the great victory you won on the ninth day of the seventh month two years ago, and so on this same month and day I am posting you to Peng Gate with the chief minister's seal.

sentences.zh: 」仍賜門戟，改鄉里為將相鄉勳賢里，九月，徐州大火，益出金、粟振之。

translations.literal: " He was also granted halberds for his gate, and his home district was renamed General-and-Minister Village, Meritorious Worthies Lane; in the ninth month a great fire struck Xuzhou, and Yi disbursed gold and grain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: " He was also granted halberds for his gate, and his home district was renamed General-and-Minister Village, Meritorious Worthies Lane. In the ninth month a great fire struck Xuzhou, and he distributed gold and grain for relief.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙鎮秦州，充西面都部署。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to govern Qin Prefecture as commander-in-chief on the western front.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Qin Prefecture as commander-in-chief on the western front.

sentences.zh: 階州義軍校王君懷苦其刺史暴虐，率眾數千投蜀，請為先鋒，下秦、成諸州。

translations.literal: Wang Junhuai, an officer of the volunteer army of Jie Prefecture, resenting his prefect's cruelty and oppression, led several thousand men to defect to Shu, asked to serve as vanguard, and descended on Qin, Cheng, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Junhuai, an officer of the volunteer army of Jie Prefecture, resenting his prefect's cruelty, led several thousand men to defect to Shu, offered to serve as vanguard, and overran Qin, Cheng, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 益聞之懼，請援於朝；

translations.literal: Yi heard of it and was afraid; he requested reinforcements from court;
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi was alarmed when he heard of it and asked the court for reinforcements;

sentences.zh: 又潛遺書於蜀將，以達誠意。

translations.literal: and also secretly sent letters to Shu generals to convey his good faith.
translations.idiomatic: and also secretly sent letters to Shu generals to declare his good faith.

sentences.zh: 少帝聞之，疑為邊患，議徙於內地。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor heard of it, he suspected a border threat and discussed moving Yi to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor heard of this, he suspected a border threat and discussed transferring him inland.

sentences.zh: 會蒲帥安審琦移鎮許下，以益為河中尹、護國軍節度。

translations.literal: When the Pu commander An Shenqi was transferred to govern below Xu, Yi was made prefect of Hezhong and military governor of the Huguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pu commander An Shenqi was transferred to Xu, Hou Yi was made prefect of Hezhong and military governor of the Huguo Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，益率僚屬歸京師，詣契丹主，自陳不預北伐之謀。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Yi led his staff back to the capital, went to the Khitan ruler, and declared that he had taken no part in the northern campaign plot.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Hou Yi led his staff to the capital, presented himself to the Khitan ruler, and declared that he had had no part in plotting the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 契丹授以鳳翔節度。

translations.literal: The Khitan appointed him military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan appointed him military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 漢祖即位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Han founder took the throne, Yi was additionally made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder took the throne, Hou Yi was additionally appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 益自以嘗受契丹命，聞漢兵入洛，憂之，浚城隍為備，孟昶遣益所親掌樞密王處回賫書招益，復遣綿州刺史吳崇惲厚遺之。

translations.literal: Yi, knowing he had once accepted Khitan appointment, was anxious when he heard Han troops had entered Luoyang; he deepened moats and walls in preparation. Meng Chang sent Wang Chuhui, whom Yi trusted and who held the Bureau of Military Affairs, with a letter to win him over, and also sent Wu Chongyun, prefect of Mian Prefecture, with lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi, knowing he had once accepted appointment from the Khitan, was anxious when he heard Han troops had entered Luoyang and strengthened his walls and moats. Meng Chang sent Wang Chuhui, whom Yi trusted and who directed the Bureau of Military Affairs, with a letter to win him over, and also sent Wu Chongyun, prefect of Mian Prefecture, with lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 崇惲本秦州押衙，益故吏也，及何重建為帥遣崇惲奉表以階、秦歸蜀，授刺史，故昶遣之。

translations.literal: Chongyun had originally been an adjutant at Qin Prefecture and was Yi's former subordinate; when He Chongjian became commander he sent Chongyun with a memorial offering Jie and Qin to Shu and was made prefect—therefore Chang sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyun had originally been an adjutant at Qin Prefecture and had been Yi's subordinate; when He Chongjian became commander he sent Chongyun with a memorial offering Jie and Qin to Shu and was made prefect—hence Chang sent him.

sentences.zh: 益遂與其子歸蜀，昶令重建率川兵數萬出大散關以應之。

translations.literal: Yi then went to Shu with his son; Chang ordered Chongjian to lead tens of thousands of Sichuan troops out through Dasanguan to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi then went to Shu with his son; Chang ordered Chongjian to lead tens of thousands of Sichuan troops through Dasanguan to support him.

sentences.zh: 漢祖知其事，遣客省使王景崇率禁軍數千，倍道趨岐下，召益入朝。

translations.literal: The Han founder learned of the affair and sent the Reception Bureau commissioner Wang Jingchong with several thousand imperial troops by forced march to Qi, summoning Yi to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder learned of this and sent the Reception Bureau commissioner Wang Jingchong with several thousand imperial troops by forced march to Qi to summon Hou Yi to court.

sentences.zh: 時漢祖已不豫，召至臥內，謂之曰：「侯益貌順朝廷，心懷攜貳。

translations.literal: The Han founder was already ill; he summoned Jingchong to his bedside and said, "Hou Yi looks compliant toward court but harbors divided loyalty in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder was already ill; he summoned Jingchong to his bedside and said, "Hou Yi looks obedient to the court but harbors divided loyalties in his heart.

sentences.zh: 爾往至彼，如益來，即置勿問；

translations.literal: When you go there, if Yi comes, set the matter aside and do not question him;
translations.idiomatic: When you arrive, if Hou Yi comes to court, leave him be;

sentences.zh: 茍遲疑不決，即以便宜從事。

translations.literal: if he hesitates and will not decide, then act at your own discretion."
translations.idiomatic: if he hesitates, act at your own discretion."

sentences.zh: 」景崇至京兆，合岐、雍、邠、涇之師以破蜀軍。

translations.literal: Jingchong reached Jingzhao, combined the armies of Qi, Yong, Bin, and Jing, and defeated the Shu forces.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong reached Jingzhao, combined the armies of Qi, Yong, Bin, and Jing, and defeated the Shu forces.

sentences.zh: 益懼，即謀入朝。

translations.literal: Yi was afraid and at once planned to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi was alarmed and at once planned to go to court.

sentences.zh: 會聞漢祖崩，景崇欲誅益，慮隱帝不知先朝密旨。

translations.literal: When he heard the Han founder had died, Jingchong wished to execute Yi but feared the Hidden Emperor did not know the previous court's secret order.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard the Han founder had died, Jingchong wished to execute Hou Yi but feared the Hidden Emperor did not know the previous emperor's secret instructions.

sentences.zh: 從事程渥，景崇里人也，益因遣之說景崇曰：「君致位通顯，亦可少知止足，何必懷禍人之心，為已甚之事乎。

translations.literal: The staff officer Cheng Wo was a fellow townsman of Jingchong; Yi therefore sent him to persuade Jingchong, saying, "You have risen to high rank and may well know when to be content—why harbor a mind to harm others and do what goes too far?
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer Cheng Wo was from Jingchong's home district; Hou Yi sent him to persuade Jingchong, saying, "You have risen to high rank and ought to know when enough is enough—why harbor murderous intent and go too far?

sentences.zh: 況侯君親戚爪牙甚眾，事若妄發，禍亦旋踵至矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Lord Hou has many kin and retainers; if the affair is rashly begun, disaster will follow at once."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Lord Hou has many kin and retainers; if you act rashly, disaster will follow at once."

sentences.zh: 」景崇怒曰：「子去，勿為遊說，吾將族爾！

translations.literal: Jingchong said angrily, "Be gone—do not lobby me; I shall exterminate your clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong said angrily, "Be gone—do not lobby me; I shall exterminate your clan!"

sentences.zh: 」益知不用渥言，即率數十騎奔入朝。

translations.literal: Yi knew Wo's words had not been heeded and at once led several dozen horsemen in a dash to court.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his plea had failed, Hou Yi at once led several dozen horsemen in a dash to court.

sentences.zh: 隱帝遣侍臣問益結連蜀軍之由，益對曰：「臣欲誘之出關，掩殺之耳。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor sent a palace attendant to ask Yi the reason for his collusion with Shu troops; Yi replied, "Your servant wished to lure them out of the pass and destroy them in an ambush."
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor sent a palace attendant to ask why he had colluded with Shu troops; Hou Yi replied, "I meant to lure them out of the pass and destroy them in an ambush."

sentences.zh: 」隱帝笑之。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor laughed at this.

sentences.zh: 益厚賂史弘肇輩，言景崇之橫恣。

translations.literal: Yi lavishly bribed Shi Hongzhao and his circle, speaking of Jingchong's arrogance and excess.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yi lavished bribes on Shi Hongzhao and his faction, accusing Jingchong of arrogance and abuse of power.

sentences.zh: 諸權貴深庇護之，乃授以開封尹兼中書令。

translations.literal: The powerful ministers deeply sheltered him, and he was then appointed prefect of Kaifeng and concurrently chief minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful ministers shielded him closely, and he was appointed prefect of Kaifeng and concurrently chief minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄封魯國公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 景崇聞之，遂據城叛，益親屬在城中餘七十口悉為景崇所害。

translations.literal: When Jingchong heard of it, he rebelled and held the city; more than seventy of Yi's kin and dependents remaining in the city were all killed by Jingchong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingchong heard of this, he rebelled and held the city; more than seventy of Hou Yi's kin and dependents still in the city were all killed by Jingchong.

sentences.zh: 及周祖起兵，隱帝議出師禦之，益獻計曰：「王者無敵於天下，兵不宜輕出，況大名戍卒家屬盡在京城，不如閉關以挫其銳，遣其母妻發降以招之，可不戰而定。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder raised troops, the Hidden Emperor discussed sending an army to resist; Yi offered a plan: "A true king has no match under Heaven; troops should not be lightly sent forth. Moreover, the families of the Daming garrison are all in the capital—better to close the passes and blunt their edge, send out their mothers and wives with offers of surrender to win them over, and settle the matter without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder raised troops, the Hidden Emperor discussed sending an army against him; Hou Yi offered a plan: "A true king has no match under Heaven; troops should not be sent out lightly. The families of the Daming garrison are all in the capital—better to close the passes and blunt their momentum, send out their mothers and wives with offers of surrender to win them over, and settle the matter without fighting."

sentences.zh: 」慕容彥超以為益衰老，作懦夫計，沮之。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao thought Yi was old and feeble and making a coward's plan, and opposed it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao thought Hou Yi was old and feeble and making a coward's plan, and opposed it.

sentences.zh: 隱帝遣益與彥超及張彥超、閻晉卿，吳虔裕守澶州。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor sent Yi with Yanchao, Zhang Yanchao, Yan Jinqing, and Wu Qianyu to hold Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Emperor sent Hou Yi with Yanchao, Zhang Yanchao, Yan Jinqing, and Wu Qianyu to hold Chun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 至赤岡，周師奄至，戰留子陂，漢軍不利。

translations.literal: At Chigang the Zhou army suddenly arrived; they fought at Liuzi Slope and the Han army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: At Chigang the Zhou army suddenly arrived; they fought at Liuzi Slope and the Han army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 益臨陣，見士卒無鬥志，又占候不祥，乃與焦繼勳等夜謁周祖，周祖慰勞遣還。

translations.literal: Yi faced the battle line, saw the soldiers had no fighting spirit, and his divinations were also inauspicious; he then visited the Zhou founder by night with Jiao Jixun and others; the Zhou founder comforted him and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle line Hou Yi saw the soldiers had no fighting spirit, and his divinations were inauspicious; he then visited the Zhou founder by night with Jiao Jixun and others; the Zhou founder comforted him and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遣賜器幣，歲一來朝，太祖以耆舊厚待之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, he sent gifts of vessels and silks; Yi came to court once a year, and the emperor treated this elder with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu took the throne, he sent gifts of vessels and silks; Hou Yi came to court once a year, and the emperor treated this elder statesman with great favor.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，郊祀，詔綴中書門下班，禮與丞相等。

translations.literal: Early in Qiande, at the suburban sacrifice, an edict placed him in the Secretariat Gate rear rank, with ritual equal to chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qiande, at the suburban sacrifice, an edict placed him in the rear rank at the Secretariat Gate, with ceremonial standing equal to chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年八十，贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged eighty, and was posthumously made chief minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, aged eighty, and was posthumously appointed chief minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五子：仁愿、仁矩、仁寶、仁遇、仁興。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Renyuan, Renju, Renbao, Renyu, and Renxing.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Renyuan, Renju, Renbao, Renyu, and Renxing.

sentences.zh: 仁愿至左金吾衛大將軍、蓬州刺史；

translations.literal: Renyuan rose to great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and prefect of Peng Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan rose to great general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and prefect of Peng Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 仁遇，西京內園使；

translations.literal: Renyu was commissioner of the Western Capital inner gardens;
translations.idiomatic: Renyu was commissioner of the Western Capital inner gardens;

sentences.zh: 仁興，右屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: Renxing was a general of the Right Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Renxing was a general of the Right Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 仁願子延濟，西京作坊使、康州刺史。

translations.literal: Renyuan's son Yanji was commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and prefect of Kang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan's son Yanji was commissioner of the Western Capital workshops and prefect of Kang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子 仁矩

translations.literal: Son: Renju
translations.idiomatic: Son: Renju

sentences.zh: 仁矩從益為商州牙校。

translations.literal: Renju followed Yi as a yamen adjutant at Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Renju followed Hou Yi as a yamen adjutant at Shang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 益之討張從賓也，仁矩首犯賊鋒，以功領蓬州刺史，充河南牙職。

translations.literal: When Yi campaigned against Zhang Congbin, Renju was first to strike the rebel van; for his merit he was made prefect of Peng Prefecture and served as Henan yamen officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Yi campaigned against Zhang Congbin, Renju was first to strike the rebel van; for his merit he was made prefect of Peng Prefecture and served as Henan yamen officer.

sentences.zh: 從益歷潞、徐、秦三鎮。

translations.literal: He followed Yi through the three postings at Lu, Xu, and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Hou Yi through his postings at Lu, Xu, and Qin.

sentences.zh: 開運初，入為氈毯使，出為天平行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyun he entered court as felt-and-carpet commissioner and went out as campaign marshal of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun he was recalled as felt-and-carpet commissioner and then posted as campaign marshal of Tianping.

sentences.zh: 漢妝，授隰州刺史，至郡決滯訟，一日釋繫囚百餘，獄為之空，民情悅服。

translations.literal: When Han was founded he was appointed prefect of Xi Prefecture; on reaching the commandery he cleared backlogged suits, and in one day released more than a hundred prisoners held in bonds—the jails were emptied thereby and the people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty was founded he was appointed prefect of Xi Prefecture; on reaching his post he cleared backlogged cases and in one day released more than a hundred prisoners—the jails were emptied and the people were pleased.

sentences.zh: 仕周，歷左羽林將軍，出為泗州刺史，改通州，兼屯田鹽鐵監使。

translations.literal: Under Zhou he served as general of the Left Forest Guard, went out as prefect of Si Prefecture, was transferred to Tong Prefecture, and concurrently served as commissioner of the farming, salt, and iron bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou he served as general of the Left Forest Guard, was posted as prefect of Si Prefecture, transferred to Tong Prefecture, and concurrently served as commissioner of farming, salt, and iron.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷祁、雄二州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Song he successively governed Qi and Xiong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he successively governed Qi and Xiong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 治軍有方略，歷數郡，咸有善政。

translations.literal: In governing troops he had method; through several commanderies he always had good administration.
translations.idiomatic: He governed troops with sound method; in every commandery he served he left a record of good administration.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，卒年五十六。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he died, aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚惜之，特命中使護喪。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu deeply regretted his loss and specially ordered a palace envoy to oversee the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu deeply regretted his loss and specially ordered a palace envoy to oversee the funeral.

sentences.zh: 子延廣、延之、咸平二年進士及弟。

translations.literal: His sons were Yanguang and Yanzhi; the latter passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yanguang and Yanzhi; the latter passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xianping.

sentences.zh: 子 仁寶

translations.literal: Son: Renbao
translations.idiomatic: Son: Renbao

sentences.zh: 仁寶以蔭遷太子中允，即趙普妹婿。

translations.literal: Renbao was transferred by yin privilege to attendant in the crown prince's household; he was also the son-in-law of Zhao Pu's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Renbao was promoted by yin privilege to attendant in the crown prince's household; he was also the son-in-law of Zhao Pu's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 盧多遜與普有隙，普罷相，即以仁寶知邕州。

translations.literal: Lu Duosun bore a grudge against Pu; when Pu was removed as chief minister, Renbao was at once made prefect of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Duosun bore a grudge against Zhao Pu; when Pu was removed as chief minister, Renbao was at once made prefect of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州之右江生毒藥樹，宣化縣人常采貨之。

translations.literal: On the prefecture's You River grew poison-drug trees; the people of Xuanhua County often gathered them for sale.
translations.idiomatic: On the prefecture's You River grew poisonous trees; the people of Xuanhua County often gathered them for sale.

sentences.zh: 仁寶以聞，詔盡伐去。

translations.literal: Renbao reported this, and an edict ordered them all cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Renbao reported this, and an edict ordered them all cut down.

sentences.zh: 九年不代。

translations.literal: For nine years he was not replaced.
translations.idiomatic: He was not replaced for nine years.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，上言陳取交州之策，太宗大喜，令馳驛召歸。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo he memorialized setting forth a plan to take Jiaozhou; Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and ordered him summoned back by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo he memorialized with a plan to take Jiaozhou; Emperor Taizong was greatly pleased and ordered him summoned back by express relay.

sentences.zh: 多遜遽奏曰：「若召仁寶，其謀必泄，蠻夷增備，未易取也。

translations.literal: Duosun hurriedly memorialized: "If Renbao is summoned, the plan will surely leak; the barbarians will increase their defenses, and it will not be easy to take the place.
translations.idiomatic: Duosun hurriedly memorialized: "If Renbao is summoned, the plan will surely leak; the barbarians will strengthen their defenses, and the place will not be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 不如授仁寶飛輓之任，且經度之，別遣偏將發荊湖士卒一二萬人，長驅而往，勢必萬全。

translations.literal: Better to give Renbao charge of rapid transport and let him plan the operation, and separately send a subordinate general to raise ten or twenty thousand troops from Jinghu and drive straight forward—the outcome will surely be wholly secure."
translations.idiomatic: Better to give Renbao charge of rapid transport and let him plan the operation, and separately send a subordinate general to raise ten or twenty thousand troops from Jinghu and drive straight forward—the outcome will surely be secure."

sentences.zh: 」帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂以仁寶為交州水陸計度轉運使。

translations.literal: Renbao was then made commissioner for planning and transport by land and water for Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Renbao was then appointed commissioner for planning and transport by land and water for Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 前軍發，遇賊鋒甚盛，援兵不繼，遇害死江中。

translations.literal: The vanguard set out, met a very strong rebel front, reinforcements did not follow up, and he was killed in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard set out, met a very strong rebel force, reinforcements failed to arrive, and he was killed in the river.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞之，甚悼惜，特贈工部侍郎，錄其子延齡、延世並為齋郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong heard of it he deeply mourned him, specially posthumously made him vice minister of the Works, and enrolled his sons Yanling and Yanshi both as ritual officers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong heard of it he deeply mourned him, posthumously appointed him vice minister of the Works, and enrolled his sons Yanling and Yanshi as ritual officers.

sentences.zh: 延齡至殿中丞。

translations.literal: Yanling rose to palace director.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling rose to palace director.

sentences.zh: 延世至太子中舍。

translations.literal: Yanshi rose to attendant in the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi rose to attendant in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 孫 延廣

translations.literal: Grandson: Yanguang
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Yanguang

sentences.zh: 延廣，初在繈褓中，遭王景崇之難，乳母劉氏以己子代延廣死。

translations.literal: Yanguang, while still in swaddling clothes, suffered Wang Jingchong's calamity; his wet nurse Lady Liu had her own son die in Yanguang's place.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang, while still an infant, suffered Wang Jingchong's massacre; his wet nurse Lady Liu had her own son die in his place.

sentences.zh: 劉氏行丐抱持延廣至京師還益。

translations.literal: Lady Liu went begging, carrying Yanguang to the capital and returning him to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu went begging, carrying Yanguang to the capital and returning him to Hou Yi.

sentences.zh: 延廣父歷通、祁、雄三州刺史，悉以補牙職。

translations.literal: Yanguang's father served successively as prefect of Tong, Qi, and Xiong, and appointed him to yamen posts in all three.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang's father served successively as prefect of Tong, Qi, and Xiong, and appointed him to yamen posts in all three.

sentences.zh: 仁矩在雄州日，方飲宴，虜數十騎白晝入州城，居民驚擾。

translations.literal: When Renju was at Xiong Prefecture, while he was at a banquet, several dozen barbarian horsemen entered the prefectural city in broad daylight and the populace was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Renju was at Xiong Prefecture, while he was at a banquet, several dozen barbarian horsemen entered the city in broad daylight and threw the populace into alarm.

sentences.zh: 延廣引親信數騎馳出衙門，射殺其酋長一人，斬首數級，悉禽其餘黨。

translations.literal: Yanguang led several trusted horsemen in a dash from the yamen gate, shot and killed one of their chiefs, took several heads, and captured all the rest of the band.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang led several trusted horsemen in a dash from the yamen gate, shot and killed one of their chiefs, took several heads, and captured the rest of the band.

sentences.zh: 延廣持首級以獻，仁矩喜，拊其背曰：「興吾門者必汝也。

translations.literal: Yanguang presented the heads; Renju was pleased, clapped his back, and said, "The one who will raise our house must be you."
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang presented the heads; Renju was pleased, clapped his back, and said, "You are the one who will raise our house."

sentences.zh: 」監軍李漢超以其事聞，詔書褒美，賜錦袍銀帶。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Li Hanchao reported the affair; an edict praised him and bestowed a brocade robe and silver belt.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Li Hanchao reported the affair; an edict praised him and bestowed a brocade robe and silver belt.

sentences.zh: 仁矩卒，補西頭供奉官。

translations.literal: When Renju died, Yanguang was appointed attendant of the western bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Renju died, Yanguang was appointed attendant of the western bureau.

sentences.zh: 從党進討太原。

translations.literal: He followed Dang Jin in the campaign against Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Dang Jin in the campaign against Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，預修永昌陵，出護延州軍兼緣邊巡檢，善撫士卒，下樂為用，戎人畏服，遷閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Early in Taiping Xingguo he took part in building the Yongchang Mausoleum, went out to guard the Yanzhou army and concurrently served as frontier inspector; he treated soldiers well, his subordinates gladly served him, the barbarians feared and submitted, and he was transferred to palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping Xingguo he took part in building the Yongchang Mausoleum, was posted to guard the Yanzhou army and serve as frontier inspector; he treated his soldiers well, his men gladly followed him, the barbarians feared and submitted, and he was transferred to palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 會西北戎入寇，邊人擾亂，求可使徼巡者。

translations.literal: When northwestern barbarians raided and border people were disturbed, the court sought someone who could patrol the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When northwestern barbarians raided and the border was thrown into turmoil, the court sought someone who could patrol the frontier.

sentences.zh: 近臣言：「延廣將家子，習邊事無出其右。

translations.literal: A court intimate said, "Yanguang is a general's son and in frontier affairs has no superior."
translations.idiomatic: A court intimate said, "Yanguang is a general's son and in frontier affairs has no superior."

sentences.zh: 」延廣時被病，強起之，遷崇儀副使，充同、鄜、坊、延、丹緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Yanguang was then ill but was roused by force, transferred to deputy commissioner of honored ritual, and made chief frontier inspector of Tong, Fu, Fang, Yan, and Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was then ill but was ordered to take the post anyway, promoted to deputy commissioner of honored ritual, and made chief frontier inspector of Tong, Fu, Fang, Yan, and Dan.

sentences.zh: 延廣力疾入辭，太宗賜以名藥及方，遣太醫隨侍，其疾亦尋愈。

translations.literal: Yanguang, forcing himself despite illness, came to take leave; Emperor Taizong bestowed famous medicines and prescriptions and sent an imperial physician to attend him, and his illness soon recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang came to take leave despite his illness; Emperor Taizong bestowed famous medicines and prescriptions and sent an imperial physician to attend him, and he soon recovered.

sentences.zh: 戎人聞延廣之至，不敢復為寇亂。

translations.literal: When the barbarians heard Yanguang had arrived, they dared not raid again.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarians heard Yanguang had arrived, they dared not raid again.

sentences.zh: 叛卒劉渥嘯聚亡命數百人，寇耀州富平縣，謀入京兆，其勢甚盛。

translations.literal: The mutineer Liu Wo gathered several hundred outlaws by rallying cry, raided Fuping County in Yao Prefecture, plotted to enter Jingzhao, and his force was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineer Liu Wo gathered several hundred outlaws, raided Fuping County in Yao Prefecture, plotted to enter Jingzhao, and his force was very strong.

sentences.zh: 所過殺居民，奪財物，縱火而去，關右騷然。

translations.literal: Where they passed they killed inhabitants, seized goods, set fires and departed, and the region west of the pass was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Where they passed they killed inhabitants, seized goods, set fires and moved on, and the region west of the pass was thrown into uproar.

sentences.zh: 延廣率兵數百，自間道追之，會渥於富平西十五里，渥眾已千餘人，相持久之。

translations.literal: Yanguang led several hundred troops by a hidden path in pursuit, met Wo fifteen li west of Fuping—Wo's band already numbered more than a thousand—and they faced each other in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang led several hundred troops by a hidden path in pursuit, met Wo fifteen li west of Fuping—Wo's band already numbered more than a thousand—and they faced each other in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 渥素憚延廣，傳言：「我草間求活，觀死如鴻毛耳；

translations.literal: Wo had always feared Yanguang and sent word: "I seek life in the grass; I regard death as lighter than a goose feather;
translations.idiomatic: Wo had always feared Yanguang and sent word: "I seek life in the wild; I regard death as lighter than a goose feather;

sentences.zh: 侯公家世富貴，奈何不思保守，而與亡卒爭一旦之命於鋒鏑之下？

translations.literal: Lord Hou's family has been rich and noble for generations—why not think of preserving yourself rather than contending with desperate men for a moment's life under blades and arrows?"
translations.idiomatic: Lord Hou's family has been rich and noble for generations—why not think of preserving yourself rather than contending with desperate men for a moment's life under blades and arrows?"

sentences.zh: 」延廣怒，因擊之，挺身與渥鬥大樹下，斷渥右臂，渥脫走，乘勢大破其眾。

translations.literal: Yanguang was angry and attacked; he stepped forward and fought Wo beneath a great tree, severed Wo's right arm, Wo broke away and fled, and Yanguang took the momentum and routed the host utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang was enraged and attacked; he stepped forward and fought Wo beneath a great tree, severed Wo's right arm, Wo broke away and fled, and Yanguang took the momentum and routed his forces utterly.

sentences.zh: 渥創甚，止谷中，後數日為追兵所獲。

translations.literal: Wo was badly wounded and halted in a valley; several days later he was taken by pursuing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wo was badly wounded and halted in a valley; several days later he was captured by pursuing troops.

sentences.zh: 渥素號驍勇無敵，至是為延廣所殺，群盜喪氣，餘黨稍稍自歸，關右以定。

translations.literal: Wo had been famed as matchlessly fierce and brave; now he was killed by Yanguang, the bandits lost heart, the remaining followers gradually surrendered of themselves, and the region west of the pass was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wo had been famed as matchlessly fierce and brave; now he was killed by Yanguang, the bandits lost heart, the remaining followers gradually surrendered, and the region west of the pass was pacified.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，擢拜崇儀使。

translations.literal: The emperor commended him and promoted him to commissioner of honored ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and promoted him to commissioner of honored ritual.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，李繼遷始擾夏臺，即命延廣領獎州刺史、知靈州，賜金帶名馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, when Li Jiqian first began to harass Xia Terrace, Yanguang was at once ordered to hold Jia Prefecture and govern Ling Prefecture, and was granted a gold belt and a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, when Li Jiqian first began to harass Xia Terrace, Yanguang was appointed prefect of Jia Prefecture and governor of Ling Prefecture, and was granted a gold belt and a famous horse.

sentences.zh: 會趙保忠陰結繼遷，朝廷命騎將李繼隆率兵問罪，以延廣護其軍。

translations.literal: When Zhao Baozhong secretly joined Jiqian, the court ordered the cavalry general Li Jilong to lead troops to punish them, with Yanguang as army protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Baozhong secretly allied with Jiqian, the court ordered the cavalry general Li Jilong to lead troops against them, with Yanguang as army protector.

sentences.zh: 既而夏臺平，保忠就縛。

translations.literal: Soon Xia Terrace was pacified and Baozhong was bound and taken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xia Terrace was pacified and Baozhong was captured.

sentences.zh: 手詔褒美，錫賚甚厚。

translations.literal: An imperial autograph edict praised him and the gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial autograph edict praised him and the rewards were very generous.

sentences.zh: 師還，留為延州鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was retained as Yanzhou commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was retained as commander at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會節帥田重進老耄，郡中不治，以延廣同知州事兼緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When the military governor Tian Chongjin was old and feeble and the commandery was poorly governed, Yanguang was made co-administrator of the prefecture and concurrently chief frontier inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When the military governor Tian Chongjin grew old and feeble and the commandery was poorly governed, Yanguang was made co-administrator of the prefecture and concurrently chief frontier inspector.

sentences.zh: 先是，延廣知靈州，部下嚴整，戎人悅服，李繼遷素避其鋒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yanguang governed Ling Prefecture, his subordinates were strict and orderly, the barbarians were pleased and submitted, and Li Jiqian had always avoided his edge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yanguang governed Ling Prefecture, his subordinates were disciplined, the barbarians were pleased and submitted, and Li Jiqian had always avoided confronting him.

sentences.zh: 監軍康贊元害其功，誣奏延廣得虜情，恐後倔強難制。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Kang Zanyuan envied his merit and falsely memorialized that Yanguang had won the barbarians' favor and might later prove stubborn and hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Kang Zanyuan envied his merit and falsely memorialized that Yanguang had won the barbarians' favor and might later prove stubborn and hard to control.

sentences.zh: 遽詔還，以慕容德豐代之，部內甚不治。

translations.literal: He was hurriedly recalled by edict and Murong Defeng replaced him; within the command the administration was very poor.
translations.idiomatic: He was hurriedly recalled by edict and Murong Defeng replaced him; the commandery was very poorly governed thereafter.

sentences.zh: 至道間，繼遷寇靈州，朝廷謀帥，同知樞密院事錢若水稱延廣可使，就拜寧州團練使、知靈州兼兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: During Zhidao, Jiqian raided Ling Prefecture; the court sought a commander, and the co-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Qian Ruoshui said Yanguang would serve; he was then appointed regimental commissioner of Ning Prefecture, governor of Ling Prefecture, and concurrently overall commander of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhidao, when Jiqian raided Ling Prefecture, the court sought a commander; the co-director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Qian Ruoshui recommended Yanguang, and he was appointed regimental commissioner of Ning Prefecture, governor of Ling Prefecture, and concurrently overall commander of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 賜白金二千兩，歲增給錢二百萬。

translations.literal: He was granted two thousand taels of white gold and an annual supplement of two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted two thousand taels of white gold and an annual supplement of two million cash.

sentences.zh: 戎人塞道，郵傳饋餫皆不通，延廣獨引數十騎之鎮，戎人素服其威名，皆相率引避。

translations.literal: The barbarians blocked the roads and postal relay and supply transport were all cut off; Yanguang alone led several dozen horsemen to the post; the barbarians had long respected his renown and all drew aside in succession to give way.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians blocked the roads and postal relay and supply transport were all cut off; Yanguang alone led several dozen horsemen to his post; the barbarians had long respected his renown and all drew aside to give way.

sentences.zh: 二年春，被病，上遣御醫馳驛視之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he fell ill; the emperor sent an imperial physician by post relay to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he fell ill; the emperor sent an imperial physician by express relay to examine him.

sentences.zh: 醫至，疾已亟，延廣謂中使李知信曰：「延廣自度必不起，家世受國恩，今日得死所矣，但恨未立尺寸功以報上耳。

translations.literal: When the physician arrived the illness was already grave; Yanguang said to the palace envoy Li Zhixin, "Yanguang judges himself unable to rise; our house has received the state's grace for generations—today I have found the place to die, but I regret only that I have not established the slightest merit to repay the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: When the physician arrived the illness was already grave; Yanguang said to the palace envoy Li Zhixin, "I know I shall not recover; our house has received the state's grace for generations—today I have found the place to die, but I regret only that I have not achieved the slightest merit to repay the sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」言訖而卒，年五十。

translations.literal: When he had spoken he died, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: When he had spoken he died, aged fifty.

sentences.zh: 上聞之為出涕，賵賻甚厚，以其子為六品正員官。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he wept; the funeral gifts were very generous and his son was made a regular sixth-rank official.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he wept; the funeral gifts were very generous and his son was made a regular sixth-rank official.

sentences.zh: 子紹隆，東染院使、帶御器械。

translations.literal: His son Shaolong was commissioner of the eastern dye works and bearer of imperial arms.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaolong was commissioner of the eastern dye works and bearer of imperial arms.

sentences.zh: 紹隆子宗亮，右侍禁、閣門祗候。

translations.literal: Shaolong's son Zongliang was right palace guard and palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shaolong's son Zongliang was right palace guard and palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 張從恩

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en

sentences.zh: 張從恩，幷州太原人。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en was a man of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en was a native of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父存信，振武軍節度。

translations.literal: His father Cunxin was military governor of the Zhenwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cunxin was military governor of the Zhenwu Army.

sentences.zh: 後唐明宗微時，嘗隸存信麾下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang was still obscure, he had once served under Cunxin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang was still obscure, he had once served under Cunxin.

sentences.zh: 時從恩尚幼，頗無賴，明宗甚薄之，及即位，止授散秩。

translations.literal: At that time Cong'en was still young and rather unruly; Mingzong thought little of him, and when he took the throne he gave him only an honorary post.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cong'en was still young and rather unruly; Mingzong thought little of him, and when he took the throne he gave him only an honorary post.

sentences.zh: 從恩不得志，乃退歸太原。

translations.literal: Cong'en could not fulfill his ambitions and therefore retired to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en could not fulfill his ambitions and retired to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 晉祖鎮河東，為少帝娶從恩女。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder governed Hedong, he took Cong'en's daughter as wife for the Young Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder governed Hedong, he took Cong'en's daughter as wife for the Young Emperor.

sentences.zh: 晉初，以外戚擢為右金吾衛將軍，未幾，改刺貝州，遷北京副留守，移授澶州防禦使。

translations.literal: Early in Jin, as an imperial in-law he was promoted to general of the Right Golden Crow Guard; before long he was made prefect of Bei Prefecture, transferred to deputy protector of the northern capital, and then made military governor of Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin dynasty, as an imperial in-law he was promoted to general of the Right Golden Crow Guard; before long he was made prefect of Bei Prefecture, transferred to deputy protector of the northern capital, and then appointed military governor of Chun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷樞密副使、宣徽南院使、權西京留守，俄判三司。

translations.literal: He served successively as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioner of the southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, acting protector of the western capital, and soon afterward as controller of the three fiscal bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioner of the southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, acting protector of the western capital, and soon afterward as controller of the three fiscal bureaus.

sentences.zh: 安從進叛於襄陽，以從恩為行營兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When An Congjin rebelled at Xiangyang, Cong'en was made overall supervisor of troops and horses of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When An Congjin rebelled at Xiangyang, Cong'en was made overall supervisor of troops and horses of the campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，襄陽平，遷檢校太尉、開封尹，充東京留守。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded, Xiangyang was pacified, and Cong'en was transferred to honorary grand marshal and prefect of Kaifeng, serving as protector of the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor succeeded, Xiangyang was pacified, and Cong'en was transferred to honorary grand marshal and prefect of Kaifeng, serving as protector of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 少帝自鄴歸汴，改鄴都留守。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor returned from Ye to Bian, Cong'en was made protector of the Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor returned from Ye to Bian, Cong'en was made protector of the Ye capital.

sentences.zh: 錫賚加等，仍賜銀裝肩輿二，俾迎其家。

translations.literal: Gifts were increased by one grade, and two silver-mounted sedan chairs were also bestowed so that he might bring his family.
translations.idiomatic: His rewards were increased by one grade, and two silver-mounted sedan chairs were also bestowed so that he might bring his family.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹擾河朔，從恩僅能完守。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan harassed Hebei; Cong'en was barely able to hold his defenses intact.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Khitan harassed Hebei; Cong'en was barely able to hold his defenses.

sentences.zh: 尋加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made co-equal chief minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made co-equal chief minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 是歲，契丹將趙延昭據甘陵，命從恩為貝州行營都部署。

translations.literal: That year the Khitan general Zhao Yanzhao held Ganling; Cong'en was ordered to be overall commander of the Bei Prefecture campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Khitan general Zhao Yanzhao held Ganling; Cong'en was ordered to be overall commander of the Bei Prefecture campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 從恩至，延昭遁去。

translations.literal: When Cong'en arrived, Yanzhao fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong'en arrived, Yanzhao fled.

sentences.zh: 詔與杜重威合兵三萬北伐。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to join Du Chongwei with thirty thousand troops in a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to join Du Chongwei with thirty thousand troops in a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 開運初，改天平軍節度。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyun he was transferred to military governor of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun he was transferred to military governor of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹復擾邊，命十五將北征，以從恩充北面行營都監。

translations.literal: The Khitan again harassed the border; fifteen generals were ordered on a northern expedition, with Cong'en as overall supervisor of the northern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan again harassed the border; fifteen generals were ordered on a northern expedition, with Cong'en as overall supervisor of the northern campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二年，移鎮晉州，又改潞州。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to govern Jin Prefecture, then again to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Jin Prefecture, then to Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及契丹入汴，從恩欲降，從事高防諫曰：「公晉室之親，宜盡臣節。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Cong'en wished to surrender; his staff officer Gao Fang remonstrated, "You are kin of the Jin house and ought to fulfill your ministerial duty."
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Cong'en wished to surrender; his staff officer Gao Fang remonstrated, "You are kin of the Jin house and ought to fulfill your ministerial duty."

sentences.zh: 」從恩不聽，乃棄城而去。

translations.literal: Cong'en would not listen and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en would not listen and abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 巡檢使王守恩悉取其家財，以城歸漢祖。

translations.literal: The inspector Wang Shou'en seized all his household property and surrendered the city to the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector Wang Shou'en seized all his household property and surrendered the city to the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 漢祖至汴。

translations.literal: The Han founder reached Bian.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder reached Bian.

sentences.zh: 從恩惶懼不敢出。

translations.literal: Cong'en was fearful and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Cong'en was fearful and did not dare come out.

sentences.zh: 漢祖召賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬、器幣以安慰之。

translations.literal: The Han founder summoned him and bestowed ceremonial robes, a gold belt, a saddled horse, and vessels and silks to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder summoned him and bestowed ceremonial robes, a gold belt, a saddled horse, and vessels and silks to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 尋拜右衛上將軍，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made senior general of the Right Guard and court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made senior general of the Right Guard and court attendant.

sentences.zh: 周初，迂左金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Zhou he was transferred to senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou dynasty he was transferred to senior general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 周祖征兗州，從恩從行。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Yan Prefecture, Cong'en accompanied the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned against Yan Prefecture, Cong'en accompanied the expedition.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，加檢校太師，封褒國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, Cong'en was given the honorary title of grand preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded, Cong'en was given the honorary title of grand preceptor and enfeoffed as Duke of Bao.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改封許國公，久之，以病免。

translations.literal: Early in Song his fief was changed to Duke of Xu; after a long time he was relieved on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song his fief was changed to Duke of Xu; after a long time he was relieved on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande he died, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 扈彥珂

translations.literal: Hu Yanke
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yanke

sentences.zh: 扈彥珂，代州雁門人。

translations.literal: Hu Yanke was a man of Yanmen in Dai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yanke was a native of Yanmen in Dai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼事王建立，以謹厚稱。

translations.literal: In youth he served Wang Jianli and was known for prudence and steadiness.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Wang Jianli and was known for prudence and steadiness.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，建立節制潞州，卒，遺表薦彥珂，得補河東節度左都押衙。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Jianli governed Lu Prefecture; when he died his final memorial recommended Yanke, who was appointed left chief adjutant of the Hedong military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Jianli governed Lu Prefecture; when he died his final memorial recommended Yanke, who was appointed left chief adjutant of the Hedong military governorship.

sentences.zh: 會漢祖自太原建號，擢為宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: When the Han founder proclaimed his reign from Taiyuan, Yanke was promoted to commissioner of the southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han founder proclaimed his reign from Taiyuan, Yanke was promoted to commissioner of the southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授鎮國軍節度，華商等州觀察、處置等使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed military governor of the Zhenguo Army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Hua, Shang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed military governor of the Zhenguo Army and commissioner for observation and disposition of Hua, Shang, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，河中李守貞、永興趙思綰、鳳翔王景崇並據城叛，周祖為樞密使，總兵出征，道出華州。

translations.literal: Early in Qianyou, Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Zhao Sizhen at Yongxing, and Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang all rebelled and held their cities; the Zhou founder was director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and led troops on campaign, passing through Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou, Li Shouzhen at Hezhong, Zhao Sizhen at Yongxing, and Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang all rebelled and held their cities; the Zhou founder was director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and led troops on campaign, passing through Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時議多以先討景崇、思綰為便，周祖意未決，彥珂曰：「三叛連衡，推守貞為主，宜先擊河中；

translations.literal: At the time opinion mostly favored first attacking Jingchong and Sizhen; the Zhou founder had not decided; Yanke said, "The three rebels are allied and make Shouzhen their leader—Hezhong should be struck first;
translations.idiomatic: At the time opinion mostly favored first attacking Jingchong and Sizhen; the Zhou founder had not decided; Yanke said, "The three rebels are allied and make Shouzhen their leader—Hezhong should be struck first;

sentences.zh: 河中平，則永興、鳳翔失勢矣。

translations.literal: when Hezhong is pacified, Yongxing and Fengxiang lose their strength.
translations.idiomatic: when Hezhong is pacified, Yongxing and Fengxiang lose their strength.

sentences.zh: 今舍近圖遠，若景崇、思綰逆戰於前，守貞兵其後，腹背受敵，為之奈何？

translations.literal: Now to abandon what is near and aim at what is far—if Jingchong and Sizhen meet us in battle in front and Shouzhen's troops come from behind, we shall be attacked front and rear—what then can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Now to abandon what is near and aim at what is far—if Jingchong and Sizhen meet us in battle in front and Shouzhen's troops come from behind, we shall be attacked front and rear—what then can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」周祖從其言，及平河中，以功遷護國軍節度。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder followed his advice; when Hezhong was pacified, Yanke was transferred to military governor of the Huguo Army for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder followed his advice; when Hezhong was pacified, Yanke was transferred to military governor of the Huguo Army for his merit.

sentences.zh: 時蒲人雕弊，思得良帥鎮撫。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Pu were worn and impoverished and longed for a good commander to pacify and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people of Pu were worn and impoverished and longed for a good commander to pacify and comfort them.

sentences.zh: 彥珂暗弱，朝議少之。

translations.literal: Yanke was dull and weak, and court opinion thought little of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanke was dull and weak, and court opinion thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 薛懷讓

translations.literal: Xue Huairang
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huairang

sentences.zh: 薛懷讓，其先戎人，徙居太原。

translations.literal: Xue Huairang's ancestors were barbarians who moved to settle at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Huairang's ancestors were barbarians who moved to settle at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 少勇敢，喜戰鬥。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave and fond of fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was brave and fond of fighting.

sentences.zh: 後唐莊宗在鎮，得隸帳下，累歷軍職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang was at his post, Huairang came under his command and rose through successive military posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Later Tang was at his post, Huairang came under his command and rose through successive military posts.

sentences.zh: 明宗時，改神武右廂都校、領獎州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mingzong he was made commander of the right wing of the Divine Martial Guard and concurrently prefect of Jiao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingzong he was made commander of the right wing of the Divine Martial Guard and concurrently prefect of Jiao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東川董璋遣懷讓率本軍從晉祖討賊，賊平，遷絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan sent Huairang to lead his own army with the Jin founder against the rebels; when the rebels were pacified he was transferred to prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan sent Huairang to lead his own army with the Jin founder against the rebels; when the rebels were pacified he was transferred to prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，移申州。

translations.literal: Early in Qingtai, he was transferred to Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai era he was transferred to Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，表乞罷郡赴代北軍，力陳不允。

translations.literal: The next year, he submitted a memorial requesting to leave his prefecture and join the northern frontier army; he argued forcefully but was not granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he memorialized asking to relinquish his prefecture and join the armies north of Dai; though he pleaded forcefully, the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，范延光叛於鄴，以懷讓為招收使。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye; Huairang was made pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Jin, when Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye, Huairang was appointed pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及戰，中流矢，詔賜湯藥存問。

translations.literal: When battle came, he was struck by a stray arrow; an edict bestowed medicinal broth and expressed concern for his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting he was hit by a stray arrow; the court sent medicinal broth and words of concern.

sentences.zh: 又歷沂、遼、密、懷四州刺史，所至無善政，頗事誅斂。

translations.literal: He then served successively as prefect of Yi, Liao, Mi, and Huai prefectures; wherever he went he showed no good governance and was much given to extortionate levies.
translations.idiomatic: He then served in turn as prefect of Yi, Liao, Mi, and Huai; nowhere did he govern well, and he was much given to extortion.

sentences.zh: 楊光遠反青州，召懷讓至闕，賜襲衣、玉帶，為行營先鋒都指揮使，以功改宿州團練使。

translations.literal: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qing Prefecture, Huairang was summoned to court, granted ceremonial robes and a jade belt, and made chief commander of the vanguard of the field headquarters; for his merit he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled at Qing Prefecture, Huairang was summoned to court, given ceremonial robes and a jade belt, and made chief commander of the campaign vanguard; for his service he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會契丹南侵，少帝幸澶州，遣懷讓與李守貞、皇甫遇、梁漢璋率兵萬人緣河而下，以守汶陽。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded southward, the Lesser Emperor went to Dan Prefecture and sent Huairang, Li Shouzhen, Huangfu Yu, and Liang Hanzhang to lead ten thousand troops downstream along the river to defend Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan invaded from the north, the Lesser Emperor went to Dan Prefecture and dispatched Huairang, Li Shouzhen, Huangfu Yu, and Liang Hanzhang with ten thousand men downstream along the river to hold Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 時契丹歲擾邊陲，朝廷擇驍將守要郡，命懷讓為洺州團練使。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan harassed the frontier year after year; the court chose fierce generals to guard key prefectures and appointed Huairang regimental commissioner of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan raided the frontier every year, and the court chose its fiercest generals for the key prefectures; Huairang was made regimental commissioner of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會符彥卿北討契丹，以懷讓為馬軍左廂排陣使。

translations.literal: When Fu Yanqing marched north against the Khitan, Huairang was made array deployment commissioner of the left wing of the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Yanqing marched north against the Khitan, Huairang was appointed array deployment commissioner of the left wing of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又從北面都招討杜重威為先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: He also followed the northern chief pacification commissioner Du Chongwei as chief commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He also served under the northern chief pacification commissioner Du Chongwei as chief commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 及重威降契丹於中渡橋，懷讓亦在籍中，非其志也。

translations.literal: When Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan at Zhongdu Bridge, Huairang was also on the rolls—against his will.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan at Zhongdu Bridge, Huairang was listed among the surrendered as well, though that was not his wish.

sentences.zh: 契丹主北歸，留麻答守鎮州，麻答遣步健督洺州供運。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler returned north, leaving Moda to guard Zhen Prefecture; Moda sent Bujian to supervise supply transport from Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler withdrew north, leaving Moda to hold Zhen Prefecture; Moda sent Bujian to oversee supply shipments from Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懷讓聞漢祖舉義晉陽。

translations.literal: Huairang heard that the Han founder had raised the standard of revolt at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huairang learned that the Han founder had risen in revolt at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 即殺步健，奉表歸漢，漢祖遣郭從義分兵萬餘，與懷讓取邢州。

translations.literal: He immediately killed Bujian, submitted a memorial pledging allegiance to Han, and the Han founder sent Guo Congyi with more than ten thousand divided troops to join Huairang in taking Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He at once killed Bujian, submitted a memorial declaring allegiance to Han, and the Han founder sent Guo Congyi with more than ten thousand troops to join Huairang in taking Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時偽帥劉鐸守邢臺，堅壁拒之，不克而還。

translations.literal: At that time the pretender commander Liu Duo held Xing city, shut the walls and resisted; they could not take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The pretender commander Liu Duo held Xing city behind stout walls and refused battle; unable to take it, they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 麻答遣副將楊安以八百騎攻懷讓，又命剛鐵將三百騎繼之。

translations.literal: Moda sent his deputy general Yang An with eight hundred cavalry to attack Huairang, and also ordered Gangtie to follow with three hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Moda sent his deputy Yang An with eight hundred horsemen against Huairang, and ordered Gangtie to follow with three hundred more.

sentences.zh: 懷讓戰不勝，退保本州，契丹大掠其封內。

translations.literal: Huairang was defeated in battle, withdrew to defend his own prefecture, and the Khitan greatly plundered his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Huairang was defeated and fell back to defend his prefecture while the Khitan plundered his domain.

sentences.zh: 及麻答為鎮軍所逐，楊安亟遁，鐸又納款漢祖。

translations.literal: When Moda was driven out by the Zhen Army, Yang An fled in haste, and Duo again submitted to the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: When Moda was driven out by the Zhen garrison, Yang An fled at once, and Duo again submitted to the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 懷讓乘其不虞，遣人紿鐸云：「我奉詔為邢州帥，今率眾襲契丹，請置頓於郡。

translations.literal: Huairang seized their unpreparedness and sent someone to deceive Duo, saying: "I have received an edict appointing me commander of Xing Prefecture; I now lead troops to strike the Khitan—please allow us to camp in the prefecture."
translations.idiomatic: Huairang took advantage of their guard being down and sent a man to deceive Duo, saying, "I have been appointed by edict commander of Xing Prefecture; I am now leading troops to strike the Khitan and ask to encamp in your prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」鐸無拒心，輒開門迎之，懷讓殺鐸，奪其城。

translations.literal: Duo had no mind to refuse and promptly opened the gates to welcome him; Huairang killed Duo and seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: Duo had no thought of refusing and opened the gates to welcome him; Huairang killed Duo and took the city.

sentences.zh: 漢祖即授以安國軍節度。

translations.literal: The Han founder immediately appointed him military governor of the Anguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder at once appointed him military governor of the Anguo Army.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，移鎮同州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yindi ascended the throne, Huairang was transferred to govern Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yindi came to the throne, Huairang was transferred to Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及殺楊邠等，急召懷讓至闕。

translations.literal: When Yang Bin and others were killed, Huairang was urgently summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Bin and the others were killed, Huairang was urgently summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 會北郊兵敗，懷讓降於周祖。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Huairang surrendered to the Zhou founder.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Huairang surrendered to the Zhou founder.

sentences.zh: 周祖登位，賜襲衣、金帶、鞍勒馬，遣還任，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder ascended the throne, he granted ceremonial robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse, sent Huairang back to his post, and added the title of provisional Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder took the throne, he granted Huairang ceremonial robes, a gold belt, and a saddled horse, sent him back to his post, and made him provisional Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 劉崇入寇，懷讓表求西征，詔褒之。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong invaded, Huairang submitted a memorial requesting to campaign westward; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong invaded, Huairang memorialized asking to march west; the court praised him in an edict.

sentences.zh: 夏陽富人張廷徽誣告趙隱等五人為盜殺人，且厚賂懷讓子有光。

translations.literal: The wealthy man of Xiayang, Zhang Tinghui, falsely accused Zhao Yin and four others of robbery and murder, and moreover heavily bribed Huairang's son Youguang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinghui, a wealthy man of Xiayang, falsely accused Zhao Yin and four others of robbery and murder, and also gave heavy bribes to Huairang's son Youguang.

sentences.zh: 懷讓知之，即諷吏掠治隱等，強伏之，遣掌書記李炳、親校賈進蒙追、判官劉震等，鍛成其獄，隱等皆棄市。

translations.literal: When Huairang learned of it, he immediately prompted officials to torture Zhao Yin and the others, forced confessions from them, and sent his chief secretary Li Bing, personal officers Jia Jin and Meng Zhui, and judicial aide Liu Zhen and others to forge the case; Zhao Yin and the others were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Huairang at once prompted officials to torture Zhao Yin and the others until they confessed, then sent his chief secretary Li Bing, personal officers Jia Jin and Meng Zhui, and judicial aide Liu Zhen and others to manufacture the case; Zhao Yin and the rest were all executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 家人詣闕訴冤，懷讓亦自入朝，遽獻錢百萬，請開宴，不納。

translations.literal: The families went to court to plead their grievances; Huairang also came to court himself and hastily offered a million in cash, requesting to host a banquet—they were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The victims' families went to court to plead their innocence; Huairang also came to court and hastily offered a million in cash, asking to host a banquet, but the gifts were refused.

sentences.zh: 俄捕獲本賊，下御史臺鞫問，懷讓懼，獻馬十匹，復不納。

translations.literal: Soon the actual culprits were captured and sent to the Censorate for interrogation; Huairang grew afraid and offered ten horses—they were again not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the real culprits were captured and interrogated by the Censorate; Huairang, afraid, offered ten horses, but they too were refused.

sentences.zh: 有司請逮懷讓繫獄，周祖以宿將，釋不問，杖流震等。

translations.literal: The responsible officials requested that Huairang be arrested and imprisoned; the Zhou founder, considering him a veteran general, released him without inquiry and had Zhen and others beaten and banished.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities asked that Huairang be arrested and imprisoned, but the Zhou founder, treating him as a veteran general, released him without punishment and had Zhen and the others beaten and banished.

sentences.zh: 俄以懷讓為左屯衛上將軍。

translations.literal: Before long Huairang was made general of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Huairang was appointed general of the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 懷讓好畜馬駝，馬有大烏小烏者，尤奇駿。

translations.literal: Huairang loved raising horses and camels; among his horses were ones called Great Crow and Little Crow, especially fine and swift.
translations.idiomatic: Huairang loved keeping horses and camels; he had horses named Great Crow and Little Crow that were especially fine and swift.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝使求之，吝而不獻。

translations.literal: Emperor Yindi of Han sent envoys to request them; he was stingy and would not surrender them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yindi of Han sent envoys to request them, but Huairang was reluctant and refused to give them up.

sentences.zh: 及罷節鎮，環衛祿薄，猶有馬百匹、橐駝三十頭，傾資以給芻粟，朝夕閱視為娛。

translations.literal: When he was removed from his military governorship, his palace guard stipend was meager, yet he still had a hundred horses and thirty camels, spending his entire fortune on fodder and grain, inspecting them morning and evening for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: After he lost his military governorship, his palace guard stipend was thin, yet he still kept a hundred horses and thirty camels, spending his whole fortune on fodder and inspecting them morning and evening for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 家人屢勸鬻以供費，懷讓不聽。

translations.literal: His family repeatedly urged him to sell them to cover expenses; Huairang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His family repeatedly urged him to sell them to meet expenses, but Huairang would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及死，童僕剺面以哭，蓋其俗也。

translations.literal: When he died, servants and retainers gashed their faces in mourning—it was their custom.
