translations.idiomatic: When he died, his servants and retainers gashed their faces in mourning, as was their custom.

sentences.zh: 趙贊，字元輔，本名美，後改焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Zan, courtesy name Yuanfu, original name Mei, later changed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zan, courtesy name Yuanfu, was originally named Mei and later changed his name.

sentences.zh: 幽州薊人。

translations.literal: A man of Ji in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was a native of Ji in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖德鈞，後唐盧龍節度，封北平王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dejun was military governor of Lulong in Later Tang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dejun was military governor of Lulong under Later Tang and was enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 父延壽，尚明宗女興平公主，至樞密使、忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: His father Yanshou married Emperor Mingzong's daughter Princess Xingping and rose to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanshou married Emperor Mingzong's daughter, Princess Xingping, and rose to director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 贊幼聰慧，明宗甚愛之，與諸子、外孫石氏並育於六宅。

translations.literal: Zan was intelligent as a child; Emperor Mingzong loved him dearly and raised him together with his own sons and the Shi clan grandsons in the Six Residences.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was clever as a child, and Emperor Mingzong loved him dearly; he was raised together with the emperor's sons and the Shi clan grandsons in the Six Residences.

sentences.zh: 暇日，因遍閱諸孫數十人，目贊曰：「是兒令器也。

translations.literal: On a day of leisure, as he looked over several dozen grandsons, he fixed his gaze on Zan and said: "This boy is promising material."
translations.idiomatic: One day of leisure, as he looked over several dozen grandsons, he fixed his eyes on Zan and said, "This boy is promising material."

sentences.zh: 」贊七歲誦書二十七卷，應神童舉。

translations.literal: At seven Zan could recite twenty-seven volumes of the classics and entered the child prodigy examination.
translations.idiomatic: At seven Zan could recite twenty-seven volumes of the classics and entered the child prodigy examination.

sentences.zh: 明宗詔曰：「都尉之子，太尉之孫，幼能誦書，弱不好弄，克彰庭訓，宜錫科名，可特賜童子及弟。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingzong issued an edict saying: "Son of a commandant, grandson of a grand commandant, able to recite the classics in youth, delicate and not fond of play, clearly reflecting family instruction—he should be granted an examination title; he is specially awarded the child prodigy jinshi degree."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong issued an edict saying, "Son of a commandant, grandson of a grand commandant, able to recite the classics in youth, delicate and not fond of play, clearly reflecting family instruction—he should be granted an examination title; he is specially awarded the child prodigy jinshi degree."

sentences.zh: 仍附長興三年禮部春榜。

translations.literal: He was also placed on the spring roster of the Ministry of Rites for the third year of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was also entered on the spring roster of the Ministry of Rites for the third year of Changxing.

sentences.zh: 」久之，延壽出鎮宣武軍，因奏署牙內都校。

translations.literal: After a long time, when Yanshou went out to govern the Xuanwu Army, he memorialized to appoint Zan as chief garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: After some time, when Yanshou went out to govern the Xuanwu Army, he memorialized to appoint Zan chief garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，晉祖起幷門，命延壽以樞密使將兵屯上黨，德鈞將本軍自幽州來會。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai, the Jin founder rose at Bingmen; he ordered Yanshou as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs to lead troops and encamp at Shangdang, and Dejun led his own army from You Prefecture to join him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qingtai the Jin founder rose at Bingmen; he ordered Yanshou, as director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, to lead troops and encamp at Shangdang, while Dejun brought his own army from You Prefecture to join him.

sentences.zh: 時晉祖以契丹之援，引兵南下，德鈞父子降晉，契丹主盡錮之北去，贊獨與母公主留西洛。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin founder, with Khitan aid, led his army south; Dejun and his son surrendered to Jin, and the Khitan ruler had them all shackled and taken north; Zan alone remained in Western Luoyang with his mother the princess.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder then, with Khitan support, marched south; Dejun and his son surrendered to Jin, and the Khitan ruler had them all shackled and taken north; Zan alone remained in Western Luoyang with his mother the princess.

sentences.zh: 天福三年，晉祖命贊奉母歸薊門，契丹署為金吾將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, the Jin founder ordered Zan to escort his mother home to Jimen; the Khitan appointed him general of the Jinwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu the Jin founder ordered Zan to escort his mother home to Jimen; the Khitan appointed him general of the Jinwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 數年，契丹以延壽為范陽節度，又署贊為牙內都校。

translations.literal: Several years later the Khitan made Yanshou military governor of Fanyang and again appointed Zan chief garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the Khitan made Yanshou military governor of Fanyang and again appointed Zan chief garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 開運末，契丹主將謀南侵，委政延壽。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, the Khitan ruler planned a southern invasion and entrusted government to Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitan ruler planned a southern invasion and entrusted affairs of state to Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 及平原陷，贊復受契丹署為河中節度。

translations.literal: When Pingyuan fell, Zan again received Khitan appointment as military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingyuan fell, Zan again received Khitan appointment as military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 延壽從契丹北歸，贊得留鎮河中。

translations.literal: Yanshou followed the Khitan north; Zan was allowed to remain governing Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou followed the Khitan north, but Zan was allowed to remain governing Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，漢祖起晉陽，贊奉表勸進，漢祖加檢校太尉，仍鎮河中。

translations.literal: Before long the Han founder rose at Taiyuan; Zan submitted a memorial urging his accession; the Han founder added the title of honorary Grand Commandant and left him governing Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Han founder rose at Taiyuan; Zan submitted a memorial urging his accession, and the Han founder added the title of honorary Grand Commandant while leaving him in command at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 改京兆尹、晉昌軍節度。

translations.literal: He was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and military governor of the Jinchang Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and military governor of the Jinchang Army.

sentences.zh: 贊懼漢疑已，潛遣親吏趙仙奉表歸蜀。

translations.literal: Zan feared Han suspicion of him and secretly sent his personal clerk Zhao Xian with a memorial submitting to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that Han would suspect him, Zan secretly sent his personal clerk Zhao Xian with a memorial submitting to Shu.

sentences.zh: 判官李恕者，本延壽賓佐，深所委賴，至家事亦參之。

translations.literal: The judicial aide Li Shu had originally been Yanshou's retainer, deeply trusted and relied upon; even household affairs were referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial aide Li Shu had originally been Yanshou's retainer and was deeply trusted; even household affairs were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 及贊出鎮，從為上介。

translations.literal: When Zan went out to govern, Shu followed as chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Zan went out to govern, Shu followed him as chief aide.

sentences.zh: 至是，恕語贊曰：「燕王入遼，非所願也，漢方建國，必務懷柔，公若泥首歸朝，必保富貴，狠狽入蜀，理難萬全。

translations.literal: At this point Shu said to Zan: "The Prince of Yan's entry into Liao was not of his own choosing; Han is just founding its state and is sure to pursue gentleness; if you prostrate yourself and return to court, wealth and honor are assured; to flee in disarray into Shu can hardly be fully safe."
translations.idiomatic: At this point Shu said to Zan, "The Prince of Yan's entry into Liao was not of his own choosing; Han is just founding its state and is sure to pursue conciliation; if you prostrate yourself and return to court, wealth and honor are assured, but to flee in disarray into Shu can hardly be fully safe."

sentences.zh: 儻復不容，後悔無及。

translations.literal: If you are again not tolerated, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If you are rejected again, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 公能聽納，請先入朝，為公申理。

translations.literal: If you can heed and accept this, let me first enter court and plead your case on your behalf.
translations.idiomatic: If you will heed this advice, let me go to court first and plead your case for you.

sentences.zh: 」贊即遣恕詣闕。

translations.literal: Zan immediately sent Shu to court.
translations.idiomatic: Zan at once sent Shu to court.

sentences.zh: 漢祖見恕，問贊何以附蜀，恕曰：「贊家在燕薊，身受契丹之命，自懷憂恐，謂陛下終不能容，招引西軍，蓋圖茍免。

translations.literal: The Han founder received Shu and asked why Zan had turned to Shu; Shu said: "Zan's family is in Yan and Ji; he bore Khitan appointments and inwardly feared and worried, thinking Your Majesty would never tolerate him; drawing western troops was merely an attempt at self-preservation."
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder received Shu and asked why Zan had turned to Shu; Shu said, "Zan's family is in Yan and Ji; he had borne Khitan appointments and feared within himself that Your Majesty would never tolerate him; drawing western troops was merely an attempt to save himself."

sentences.zh: 臣意國家甫定，務安臣民，所以令臣乞哀求覲。

translations.literal: It is my understanding that the state has just been established and seeks to reassure subjects and people; therefore I beg tearfully to request an audience.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the state has only just been established and seeks to reassure its subjects and people; therefore I beg tearfully to request an audience.

sentences.zh: 」漢祖曰：「贊之父子亦吾人也，事契丹出於不幸。

translations.literal: The Han founder said: "Zan and his father are also our people; serving the Khitan arose from misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder said, "Zan and his father are also our people; serving the Khitan arose from misfortune."

sentences.zh: 今聞延壽落於陷穽，吾忍不容贊耶？

translations.literal: Now I hear Yanshou has fallen into a trap—how could I bear not to tolerate Zan?
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear Yanshou has fallen into a trap—how could I bear not to tolerate Zan?

sentences.zh: 」恕未還，贊已離鎮入朝，即命為左驍衛上將軍，徙恕邠州判官。

translations.literal: Before Shu returned, Zan had already left his post and entered court; he was immediately appointed general of the Left Brave Guard, and Shu was transferred to judicial aide of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before Shu returned, Zan had already left his post and entered court; he was at once appointed general of the Left Brave Guard, and Shu was transferred to judicial aide of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贊仕周，歷左右羽林、左龍武三統軍。

translations.literal: Zan served Zhou and successively held command of the Left and Right Forest Guards and the Left Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, Zan successively commanded the Left and Right Forest Guards and the Left Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗南征，初遣贊率師巡警壽州城外，俄命為淮南道行營左廂排陣使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong marched south, he first sent Zan to lead troops on patrol outside Shou Prefecture; soon he was made array deployment commissioner of the left wing of the Huainan Circuit field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong marched south, he first sent Zan to lead troops on patrol outside Shou Prefecture; soon Zan was made array deployment commissioner of the left wing of the Huainan Circuit field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 世宗歸京，留贊與諸將分兵圍壽春，贊獨當東面。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong returned to the capital, he left Zan with the other generals to divide forces and besiege Shouchun; Zan alone held the eastern face.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong returned to the capital, he left Zan with the other generals to divide their forces and besiege Shouchun; Zan alone held the eastern sector.

sentences.zh: 諸將戰多不利，贊獨持重，自秋涉冬，未嘗挫衄。

translations.literal: The other generals met with many setbacks in battle; Zan alone held firm, from autumn through winter, never suffering defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The other generals met with many setbacks in battle, but Zan alone held firm; from autumn through winter he never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 及受詔移軍，尺椽片瓦，悉輦而行，城中人無敢睥睨者。

translations.literal: When he received orders to shift his army, every rafter and tile was carted away; no one in the city dared even to look askance.
translations.idiomatic: When he received orders to shift his army, every rafter and tile was carted away, and no one in the city dared even to look askance.

sentences.zh: 會吳遣驍將魯公綰帥十餘萬眾泝淮奄至，跨山為柵，阻肥水，俯瞰城中。

translations.literal: When Wu sent the fierce general Lu Gongwan leading more than a hundred thousand men upstream on the Huai to arrive suddenly, they built palisades straddling the hills, blocked the Fei River, and looked down on the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then sent the fierce general Lu Gongwan with more than a hundred thousand men upstream on the Huai to arrive suddenly; they built palisades across the hills, blocked the Fei River, and looked down on the city.

sentences.zh: 時大軍已解圍，贊與大將楊承信將輕騎斷吳人饟路，又獨以所部襲破公綰軍，為流矢所中。

translations.literal: By then the main army had lifted the siege; Zan and the great general Yang Chengxin led light cavalry to cut off the Wu supply lines, and Zan alone with his own division struck and broke Gongwan's army, but was hit by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: By then the main army had lifted the siege; Zan and the great general Yang Chengxin led light cavalry to cut Wu supply lines, and Zan alone with his own division struck and broke Gongwan's army, though he was hit by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 世宗再征壽春，命造橋渦口，以通濠、泗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong marched against Shouchun again, he ordered a bridge built at Wokou to connect Hao and Si.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong marched against Shouchun again, he ordered a bridge built at Wokou to connect Hao and Si.

sentences.zh: 令騎帥韓令坤董其役，俾贊副之。

translations.literal: He ordered the cavalry commander Han Lingkun to oversee the work and had Zan assist him.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the cavalry commander Han Lingkun to oversee the work and had Zan assist him.

sentences.zh: 屬霖雨淮水漲溢，濠人謀乘輕舟奄焚其橋，贊覘知之，設伏橋下。

translations.literal: During seasonal rains the Huai River swelled and overflowed; the people of Hao planned to take light boats and burn the bridge by surprise; Zan learned of it through reconnaissance and set an ambush beneath the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: During the rainy season the Huai River swelled and overflowed; the people of Hao planned to take light boats and burn the bridge by surprise, but Zan learned of it through reconnaissance and set an ambush beneath the bridge.

sentences.zh: 濠人果至，贊令強弩亂發，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: The people of Hao came as expected; Zan ordered crossbows to fire in disorder, killing and capturing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Hao came as expected; Zan ordered his crossbowmen to fire at will, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 及世宗移兵趣濠，以牛革蒙大盾攻城，贊親督役，矢集於胄，中被重傷，猶力戰，遂拔其羊馬城，刺史唐景思死焉，團練使郭廷請以城降。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong shifted troops toward Hao, they covered great shields with ox hide to assault the walls; Zan personally supervised the work; arrows clustered on his helmet and he was seriously wounded in the chest, yet he fought on fiercely, took the outer sheep-and-horse wall, Prefect Tang Jingsi died in the fighting, and regimental commissioner Guo Tingqing surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong shifted troops toward Hao, they covered great shields with ox hide to assault the walls; Zan personally supervised the work; arrows clustered on his helmet and he was seriously wounded in the chest, yet he fought on fiercely, took the outer sheep-and-horse wall, Prefect Tang Jingsi died in the fighting, and regimental commissioner Guo Tingqing surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔褒美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 又以所部兵巡撫滁、和之間，破吳人五百於石潭橋。

translations.literal: He also led his own troops on patrol between Chu and He, defeating five hundred Wu troops at Shitan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He also led his own troops on patrol between Chu and He and defeated five hundred Wu troops at Shitan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，以戰功多，授保信軍節度。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, for his many battle merits he was appointed military governor of the Baoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, for his many battle merits he was appointed military governor of the Baoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 贊入視事，盡去苛政，務從寬簡，居民便之。

translations.literal: When Zan entered to take up his duties, he removed all harsh policies and strove for leniency and simplicity; the residents found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Zan took up his post, he removed all harsh policies and strove for leniency and simplicity, to the residents' benefit.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加開府階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, he was granted the rank of commissioner of a capital office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi came to the throne, Zan was granted the rank of commissioner of a capital office.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加檢校太師，移忠正軍節度，預平維揚。

translations.literal: Early in Song he was made honorary Grand Preceptor, transferred to military governor of the Zhongzheng Army, and participated in the pacification of Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made honorary Grand Preceptor, transferred to military governor of the Zhongzheng Army, and took part in the pacification of Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改鎮延州，受密旨許以便宜行事。

translations.literal: After a little over a year he was transferred to govern Yan Prefecture and received a secret edict permitting him to act at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year he was transferred to Yan Prefecture and received a secret edict permitting him to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 將及州境，乃前後分置步騎，綿綿不絕，林莽之際，遠見旌旗，所部羌、渾來迎，無不懾服。

translations.literal: As he neared the prefectural border, infantry and cavalry were deployed before and behind in an unbroken stream; amid the forests and brush, banners could be seen from afar; the Qiang and Hun under his command came to welcome him, and none failed to be awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: As he neared the prefectural border, infantry and cavalry were deployed before and behind in an unbroken stream; amid the forests and brush banners could be seen from afar, and the Qiang and Hun under his command came to welcome him, all awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 乾德六年，移建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qiande he was transferred to military governor of the Jianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Qiande he was transferred to military governor of the Jianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 秋，命將征太原，以贊為邠州路部署。

translations.literal: In autumn, when an expedition against Taiyuan was ordered, Zan was made deployment commissioner of the Bin Prefecture route.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when an expedition against Taiyuan was ordered, Zan was made deployment commissioner of the Bin Prefecture route.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，太祖將討晉陽，又以為河東道行營前軍馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, when Taizu was about to attack Jinyang, Zan was again made chief adjutant of the vanguard horse and foot armies of the Hedong Circuit field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, when Taizu was about to attack Jinyang, Zan was again made chief adjutant of the vanguard horse and foot armies of the Hedong Circuit field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 車駕薄城下，分軍四面，贊扼其西偏。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage drew near beneath the walls, the army was divided on four sides; Zan held the western flank.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage drew near beneath the walls, the army was divided on four sides and Zan held the western flank.

sentences.zh: 幷人乘晦自突門潛犯贊壘，贊率眾擊之，久而方退，弩矢貫足。

translations.literal: The Bing men took advantage of darkness to steal out through the sally port and secretly attack Zan's camp; Zan led his troops to repel them; only after a long fight did they withdraw; a crossbow bolt pierced his foot.
translations.idiomatic: The Bing men took advantage of darkness to steal out through the sally port and secretly attack Zan's camp; Zan led his troops to repel them, and only after a long fight did they withdraw; a crossbow bolt pierced his foot.

sentences.zh: 太祖勞問數四，賜良藥傅之。

translations.literal: Taizu repeatedly expressed concern and reward, and bestowed fine medicine to dress the wound.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu repeatedly expressed his concern and bestowed fine medicine to dress the wound.

sentences.zh: 四年，議鎮鄜州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year it was proposed that he govern Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year it was proposed that he govern Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 贊頗知書，喜為詩，容止閑雅，接士大夫以禮，馭眾有方略。

translations.literal: Zan was fairly learned, fond of composing poetry, graceful and refined in bearing, received scholar-officials with courtesy, and had strategy in commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was fairly learned and fond of composing poetry; graceful and refined in bearing, he received scholar-officials with courtesy and had strategy in commanding troops.

sentences.zh: 其為政雖無異跡，而吏民畏服，亦近代賢帥也。

translations.literal: Though his governance showed no extraordinary traces, officials and people alike feared and respected him—he was among the worthy commanders of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Though his governance showed no extraordinary feats, officials and people alike feared and respected him; he was among the worthy commanders of recent times.

sentences.zh: 李繼勳

translations.literal: Li Jixun
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixun

sentences.zh: 李繼勳，大名元城人。

translations.literal: Li Jixun was a man of Yuancheng in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixun was a native of Yuancheng in Daming.

sentences.zh: 周祖領鎮，選隸帳下。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder held his post, Jixun was selected to serve under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder held his military post, Jixun was selected to serve under his command.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，補禁軍列校，累遷至虎捷左廂都指揮使、領永州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangshun era, he was appointed as a company commander in the imperial guard; through successive promotions he rose to commander of the left wing of the Tiger Dash Guard and concurrently served as defense commissioner of Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he joined the imperial guard as a company commander and rose through successive promotions to commander of the left wing of the Tiger Dash Guard, concurrently serving as defense commissioner of Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，遷侍衛步軍都指揮使、領昭武軍節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiande era, he was transferred to commander of the Palace Infantry Guard and concurrently made military commissioner of the Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era he was promoted to commander of the Palace Infantry Guard and concurrently appointed military commissioner of the Zhaowu Army.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改領曹州。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was reassigned to govern Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a little over a year he was reassigned to govern Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世宗親征淮上，令繼勳領兵屯壽州城南，進洞屋、雲梯，以攻其城。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally campaigned on the Huai, he ordered Jixun to lead troops and encamp south of Shou Prefecture city, advancing tunnel-approaches and cloud ladders to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong personally campaigned on the Huai River, he ordered Jixun to lead troops to encamp south of Shou Prefecture and advance tunnel-approaches and siege towers to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 繼勳怠於守禦，為其所敗，死者數萬，梯、屋悉皆被焚。

translations.literal: Jixun was slack in defense and was defeated by the enemy; tens of thousands died, and the ladders and tunnel-approaches were all burned.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun had been negligent in his defenses and was routed; tens of thousands were killed, and the siege ladders and tunnel-approaches were burned to ashes.

sentences.zh: 召歸闕，出為河陽三城節度。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital and sent out as military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and appointed military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 議者以為失責帥之義。

translations.literal: Commentators held that this fell short of the principle by which a commander should be held accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that this failed to uphold the principle of holding a commander accountable for defeat.

sentences.zh: 及再幸壽春回，左授繼勳右武衛大將軍，又以其掌書記陳南金裨贊無狀，並黜之。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from his second visit to Shouchun, Jixun was demoted to grand general of the Right Martial Guard; because his chief secretary Chen Nanjin had assisted him without merit, both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned from his second visit to Shouchun, Jixun was demoted to grand general of the Right Martial Guard; his chief secretary Chen Nanjin, who had assisted him without distinction, was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was given the additional title of honorary grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song dynasty he was given the additional title of honorary grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 太祖平澤、潞，繼勳朝於行在，即以為昭義軍節度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu pacified Ze and Lu, Jixun attended the emperor at the field headquarters and was immediately made military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu pacified Ze and Lu, Jixun came to pay court at the field headquarters and was immediately appointed military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 是秋，率師入河東，燔平遙縣，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: That autumn he led his army into Hedong, burned Pingyao County, and took many captives and booty.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he led his army into Hedong, burned Pingyao County, and took a great many captives and spoils.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，冬，又敗幷軍千餘人，斬首百餘級，獲其遼州刺史傅延彥及弟延勳來獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, in winter, he again defeated more than a thousand Bing troops, took over a hundred heads, captured their Liaozhou prefect Fu Yanyan and his younger brother Yanxun, and presented them as captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Jianlong he again routed more than a thousand Bing troops, took over a hundred heads, and captured Liaozhou prefect Fu Yanyan and his younger brother Yanxun, whom he sent in as captives.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，詔與康延沼、尹訓率步騎萬餘攻遼州，太原將郝貴超領兵來援，戰於城下，繼勳大敗之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande, an edict ordered him together with Kang Yanzhao and Yin Xun to lead more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Liaozhou; Taiyuan general Hao Guichao led troops to relieve the city; they fought beneath the walls and Jixun routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he was ordered together with Kang Yanzhao and Yin Xun to lead more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry against Liaozhou; when Taiyuan general Hao Guichao marched to relieve the city, Jixun routed his forces beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 州將杜延韜危蹙，與拱衛都指揮使冀進、兵馬都監供奉官侯美籍部下兵三千送欵於繼勳。

translations.literal: The prefectural commander Du Yantao, pressed to extremity, together with Guard commander Ji Jin and horse-and-army overseer palace attendant Hou Mei registered three thousand troops under their command and submitted in surrender to Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural commander Du Yantao, hard pressed, together with Guard commander Ji Jin and horse-and-army overseer Hou Mei, a palace attendant, registered three thousand men under their command and surrendered to Jixun.

sentences.zh: 即遣內供奉官都知慕容延忠入奏，詔褒之。

translations.literal: He immediately dispatched Inner Palace Attendant and Director Murong Yanzhong to report to the throne; an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately sent Inner Palace Attendant and Director Murong Yanzhong to report to the throne, and the emperor issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，幷人誘契丹步騎六萬人來取遼州，復遣繼勳與羅彥瓌、郭進、曹彬等領六萬眾赴之，大破契丹及太原軍於城下。

translations.literal: Before long the Bing people induced sixty thousand Khitan infantry and cavalry to come and seize Liaozhou; Jixun was again dispatched together with Luo Yangui, Guo Jin, Cao Bin, and others at the head of sixty thousand men to meet them, and beneath the city walls he routed the Khitan and Taiyuan armies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Bing induced sixty thousand Khitan troops to march on Liaozhou; Jixun was again sent with Luo Yangui, Guo Jin, Cao Bin, and others at the head of sixty thousand men, and beneath the city walls he inflicted a crushing defeat on the Khitan and Taiyuan forces.

sentences.zh: 五年，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given the additional title of co-director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made co-director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，將征河東，以繼勳為行營前軍都部署，敗幷人於渦河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao, when a campaign against Hedong was planned, Jixun was made chief deployments officer of the advance army of the field headquarters and defeated the Bing people at the Wo River.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaibao, as a campaign against Hedong was being prepared, Jixun was appointed chief deployments officer of the field headquarters advance army and defeated the Bing forces at the Wo River.

sentences.zh: 二年，太祖親征河東，命繼勳為行營前軍都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year Emperor Taizu personally campaigned against Hedong and appointed Jixun chief deployments officer of the advance army of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Emperor Taizu personally campaigned against Hedong and appointed Jixun chief deployments officer of the field headquarters advance army.

sentences.zh: 駕至城下，分軍四面，繼勳柵其南。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached beneath the city walls, the army was divided on four sides; Jixun encamped with palisades on the south.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached the city he divided his forces on four sides; Jixun established a fortified camp on the south.

sentences.zh: 三年春，移鎮大名。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he was transferred to govern Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he was transferred to govern Daming.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was additionally made palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he was additionally appointed palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 俄以疾求歸洛陽，許之，賜錢千萬、白金萬兩。

translations.literal: Soon, on grounds of illness he requested to return to Luoyang; permission was granted, and he was given ten million coins and ten thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing illness, he asked to retire to Luoyang; the request was granted, and he was given ten million coins and ten thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 是秋，上表乞骸骨，拜太子太師致仕，朝會許綴中書門下班。

translations.literal: That autumn he submitted a memorial begging to resign his bones; he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office; at court assemblies he was permitted to join the rear of the Chancellery roster.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and allowed to retire, and at court assemblies he was permitted to take his place at the rear of the Chancellery roster.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年六十二，贈中書令。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, aged sixty-two; posthumously he was given the title of Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward at the age of sixty-two and was posthumously invested as Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 繼勳累歷藩鎮，所至無善政，然以質直稱。

translations.literal: Jixun served repeatedly in regional commands; wherever he went he had no good governance, yet he was known for straightforwardness.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun served repeatedly in regional commands and achieved no notable governance wherever he went, yet he was esteemed for his straightforward character.

sentences.zh: 信奉釋氏。

translations.literal: He believed in and followed Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: He was a devout follower of Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 與太祖有舊，故特承寵遇。

translations.literal: He had an old association with Emperor Taizu and therefore received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: He had long-standing ties with Emperor Taizu and therefore enjoyed special favor at court.

sentences.zh: 弟繼偓，亦有武勇，周顯德末，補內殿直。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jiwo also had martial valor; at the end of Zhou Xiande he was appointed to the Inner Hall Direct Corps.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jiwo was also a man of martial valor; at the end of the Zhou Xiande era he was appointed to the Inner Hall Direct Corps.

sentences.zh: 宋初，累歷軍職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he successively held military posts.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song dynasty he rose through a series of military posts.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，為步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he served as deputy chief of the infantry army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he served as deputy chief of the infantry army.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，遷內外馬步軍副都軍頭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was transferred to deputy chief of the inner and outer horse and infantry armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo he was promoted to deputy chief of the inner and outer horse and infantry armies.

sentences.zh: 坐事改右衛率府率。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was changed to captain of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After a disciplinary offense he was reduced to captain of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，加本衛將軍、領獎州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was additionally made a general of his guard and concurrently made prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was additionally made a general of his guard and concurrently appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累至龍衛右廂都指揮使、領本州團練使。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he rose to commander of the right wing of the Dragon Guard and concurrently served as regimental trainer of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he rose to commander of the right wing of the Dragon Guard and concurrently served as regimental trainer of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 繼勳子守恩至如京使；

translations.literal: Jixun's son Shou'en rose to Palace Messenger for Capital Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Jixun's son Shou'en rose to the post of Palace Messenger for Capital Affairs;

sentences.zh: 守元至北作坊使；

translations.literal: Shouyuan rose to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops;
translations.idiomatic: Shouyuan rose to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops;

sentences.zh: 守徽為崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Shouhui served as Vice Commissioner of the Lofty Ceremonies Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhui served as Vice Commissioner of the Lofty Ceremonies Office.

sentences.zh: 藥元福

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanfu

sentences.zh: 藥元福，幷州晉陰人。

translations.literal: Yao Yuanfu was a man of Jinyin in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanfu was a native of Jinyin in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼有膽氣，善騎射。

translations.literal: From youth he had courage and mettle and was skilled in horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bold and spirited and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 初事邢帥王檀為廳頭軍使，以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: At first he served Xing governor Wang Tan as a hall-head army commander and was known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served Xing governor Wang Tan as a hall-head army commander and was known for his bravery.

sentences.zh: 事後唐，為拱衛、威和親從馬鬥軍都校，天平軍內外馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Serving Later Tang, he was a company commander of the Guard and Weihe intimate-follower horse guard, and commander of the inner and outer horse armies of the Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Tang he served as a company commander of the Guard and Weihe intimate-follower horse guard, and as commander of the inner and outer horse armies of the Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，為深州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Tianfu era of Jin he served as prefect of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin he served as prefect of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開運初，契丹陷甘陵，圍魏郡，師次於河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun the Khitan took Ganling and besieged Wei commandery; the army halted at the river.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyun the Khitan captured Ganling and besieged Wei commandery, and the imperial army halted at the river.

sentences.zh: 少帝駐軍澶淵，契丹陣於城北，東西連亙，掩城兩隅，登陴望之，不見其際。

translations.literal: Emperor Shao encamped at Chanyuan; the Khitan formed battle lines north of the city, extending east and west, covering both corners of the city; mounting the battlements to look, one could not see their end.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shao encamped at Chanyuan; the Khitan drew up their lines north of the city, stretching endlessly east and west and covering both corners of the walls; from the battlements one could not see where their ranks ended.

sentences.zh: 元福以左千牛衛將軍領兵居陣東偏。

translations.literal: Yuanfu, as general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard, led troops stationed on the eastern flank of the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu, commanding troops as general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard, held the eastern flank of the line.

sentences.zh: 澶民有馬破龍者告契丹曰：「先攻其東，即浮梁可奪。

translations.literal: A man of Chanyuan named Ma Polong told the Khitan: "If you attack the east first, the pontoon bridge can be seized.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Chanyuan named Ma Polong told the Khitan: "If you attack the east first, the pontoon bridge can be seized.

sentences.zh: 」契丹信之，盡銳來戰。

translations.literal: " The Khitan believed him and came to battle with all their elite forces.
translations.idiomatic: " The Khitan took him at his word and committed their full strength to the assault.

sentences.zh: 元福與慕容鄴各領二百騎為一隊，躍出而鬥，元福奮鐵撾擊契丹，斃者數人，左右馳突，無不披靡，契丹兵潰。

translations.literal: Yuanfu and Murong Ye each led two hundred cavalry as one unit, leaped out and fought; Yuanfu swung an iron mace against the Khitan and felled several men; charging left and right, none could stand before him; the Khitan army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu and Murong Ye each led a two-hundred-man cavalry unit in a charge; Yuanfu swung an iron mace and felled several Khitan warriors, then drove through their ranks in every direction until none could stand before him and the Khitan army broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 少帝登城，見元福力戰，召撫之曰：「汝奮不顧命，雖古之忠烈無以過之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shao mounted the wall, saw Yuanfu fighting fiercely, summoned and comforted him, saying: "You fight without regard for your life—even the loyal martyrs of antiquity could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shao mounted the wall and, seeing Yuanfu fighting with such ferocity, summoned him and said: "You fight as if life meant nothing—even the greatest heroes of antiquity could not surpass you.

sentences.zh: 」元福三馬皆中流矢，少帝擇名馬賜之。

translations.literal: " All three of Yuanfu's horses had been struck by arrows; Emperor Shao selected fine horses and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: " All three of Yuanfu's horses had been wounded by arrows; the emperor selected fine horses and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 明日將戰，面授元福鄭州刺史，為權臣所沮，止刺原州，俄改泰州。

translations.literal: The next day, on the eve of battle, he personally appointed Yuanfu prefect of Zheng Prefecture; obstructed by a powerful minister, he was permitted only to govern Yuan Prefecture, and soon was transferred to Tai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, on the eve of battle, the emperor personally appointed Yuanfu prefect of Zheng Prefecture; blocked by a powerful minister, he was given only Yuan Prefecture, and soon was transferred to Tai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，契丹復入。

translations.literal: The next year the Khitan invaded again.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Khitan invaded again.

sentences.zh: 命元福與李守貞、符彥卿、皇甫遇、張彥澤等禦之於陽城，為右廂副排陣使。

translations.literal: Yuanfu was ordered together with Li Shouzhen, Fu Yanqing, Huangfu Yu, Zhang Yanze, and others to meet them at Yangcheng; he served as deputy battle-array officer of the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was ordered together with Li Shouzhen, Fu Yanqing, Huangfu Yu, Zhang Yanze, and others to meet the invaders at Yangcheng, serving as deputy battle-array officer of the right wing.

sentences.zh: 晉師列方陣，設拒馬為行砦。

translations.literal: The Jin army formed a square battle formation and set up caltrop barriers as a field camp.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army formed a square battle formation and erected caltrop barriers as a marching encampment.

sentences.zh: 契丹以奇兵出陣後，斷糧道，晉人乏水，士馬饑渴，鑿井未及泉，土輒壞塞，契丹順風揚塵，諸將皆曰：「彼勢甚銳，俟風反與戰，破之必矣。

translations.literal: The Khitan sent a surprise force around behind the battle line and cut the supply route; the Jin were short of water; men and horses were hungry and thirsty; when they dug wells they had not yet reached spring water before the earth collapsed and filled in; the Khitan raised dust with the wind at their backs; all the generals said: "Their momentum is very sharp—wait until the wind turns, then fight, and they will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent a flanking force behind the Jin lines and cut their supply route; the Jin were short of water, and men and horses were parched with hunger and thirst; wells caved in before they reached water; with the wind at their backs the Khitan raised blinding dust; the generals all said: "The enemy's momentum is too strong—wait until the wind shifts, then fight, and we are sure to break them.

sentences.zh: 」守貞與元福謀曰：「軍中饑渴已甚，若俟風反出戰，吾屬為虜矣！

translations.literal: " Shouzhen and Yuanfu consulted, saying: "Within the army hunger and thirst are already extreme—if we wait for the wind to turn before fighting, we shall all become captives!
translations.idiomatic: " Shouzhen and Yuanfu conferred: "The men are already desperate with hunger and thirst—if we wait for the wind to shift before we fight, we shall all be taken captive!

sentences.zh: 彼謂我不能逆風以戰，宜出其不意以擊之，此兵家之奇也。

translations.literal: They think we cannot fight against the wind; we should strike them unexpectedly—this is a stratagem of the military art.
translations.idiomatic: They assume we dare not fight into the wind; we should strike when they least expect it—that is the kind of surprise the art of war demands.

sentences.zh: 」元福乃率麾下騎，開拒馬出戰，諸將繼至，契丹大敗，追北二十餘里，殺獲甚眾，敵帥與百餘騎遁去。

translations.literal: " Yuanfu then led the cavalry under his command, opened the caltrop barriers, and went out to battle; the other generals followed; the Khitan were utterly routed; they pursued north more than twenty li; kills and captures were very numerous; the enemy commander fled with a little over a hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanfu then led his cavalry through the caltrop barriers and charged; the other generals followed, and the Khitan were routed; the Jin pursued them more than twenty li, inflicting heavy casualties; the enemy commander fled with barely a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 以元福為威州刺史。

translations.literal: Yuanfu was made prefect of Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was appointed prefect of Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會靈武節度王令溫以漢法治蕃部，西人苦之，共謀為亂，三族酋長拓跋彥超、石存、乜廝褒率眾攻靈州。

translations.literal: When Lingwu military commissioner Wang Lingwen governed the tribal peoples by Han law, the western peoples suffered under it; they jointly plotted rebellion; the chieftains of three tribes—Tuoba Yanchao, Shi Cun, and Nie Sichou—led their followers to attack Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingwu military commissioner Wang Lingwen governed the tribal peoples by Han law, the western peoples suffered under it; they jointly plotted rebellion, and the chieftains of three tribes—Tuoba Yanchao, Shi Cun, and Nie Sichou—led their followers in an attack on Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 令溫遣人間道入奏，乃以河陽節度馮暉鎮朔方，召關右兵進討，以元福將行營騎兵。

translations.literal: Lingwen sent a man by a secret route to report to the throne; thereupon Heyang military commissioner Feng Hui was posted to garrison Shuofang; troops from west of the Pass were summoned for a punitive advance; Yuanfu was made to command the cavalry of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen sent word to the throne by a secret route; Feng Hui, military commissioner of Heyang, was posted to garrison Shuofang, troops from west of the Pass were called up for a punitive campaign, and Yuanfu was appointed to command the field headquarters cavalry.

sentences.zh: 元福與暉出威州土橋西，遇彥超兵七千餘，邀暉行李。

translations.literal: Yuanfu and Hui, marching west from Tuqiao in Wei Prefecture, encountered more than seven thousand of Yanchao's troops, who intercepted Hui's baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu and Hui marched west from Tugiao in Wei Prefecture and encountered more than seven thousand of Yanchao's troops, who waylaid Hui's baggage train.

sentences.zh: 元福轉戰五十里，殺千級，禽三十餘人，又遣部校援出令溫，護送洛下。

translations.literal: Yuanfu fought retreating battles for fifty li, killed a thousand odd, captured more than thirty men, and also dispatched a subordinate officer to relieve Lingwen and escort him to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu fought a running battle for fifty li, killing a thousand of the enemy and taking more than thirty prisoners; he also sent a subordinate officer to rescue Lingwen and escort him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朔方距威州七百里，無水草，號旱海，師須賫糧以行，至耀德食盡，比明，行四十里。

translations.literal: Shuofang was seven hundred li from Wei Prefecture; there was no water or fodder—it was called the Dry Sea; the army had to carry provisions to march; when they reached Yaode their food was exhausted; by dawn they had marched forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang lay seven hundred li from Wei Prefecture across a waterless wasteland known as the Dry Sea, and the army had to carry its own provisions; by the time they reached Yaode their food was gone, and by dawn they had marched another forty li.

sentences.zh: 彥超等眾數萬，布為三陣，扼要路，據水泉，以待暉軍，軍中大懼。

translations.literal: Yanchao and the others numbered tens of thousands; they deployed in three battle lines, blocked the vital route, seized the water springs, and waited for Hui's army; within the army fear was great.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao's forces numbered in the tens of thousands; they deployed in three lines, blocked the vital pass, held the water springs, and awaited Hui's army; great fear spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 暉遣人賂以金帛，求和解，彥超許之。

translations.literal: Hui sent men with gold and silks as bribes to seek a settlement; Yanchao agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent envoys bearing gold and silks to negotiate a settlement, and Yanchao agreed.

sentences.zh: 使者往復數四，至日中，列陣如故。

translations.literal: Envoys went back and forth several times; by midday the battle lines stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys shuttled back and forth repeatedly, yet by midday the enemy lines remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元福曰：「彼知我軍饑渴，邀我於險，既許和解而日中未決，此豈可信哉？

translations.literal: Yuanfu said: "They know our army is hungry and thirsty, and have waylaid us in perilous ground; having promised a settlement yet failing to decide by midday—how can this be trusted?
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu said: "They know our men are starving and parched and have trapped us on difficult ground; they promised peace yet by midday nothing is settled—how can we trust them?

sentences.zh: 欲困我耳。

translations.literal: They intend merely to wear us down.
translations.idiomatic: They mean only to wear us down.

sentences.zh: 遷延至暮，則吾黨成禽矣。

translations.literal: If we delay until evening, our men will become captives.
translations.idiomatic: If we delay until nightfall, we shall all be taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 」暉驚曰：「奈何？

translations.literal: " Hui said in alarm: "What is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: " Hui exclaimed in alarm: "What are we to do?

sentences.zh: 」元福曰：「彼雖眾而精兵絕少，依西山為陣者是也，餘不足患。

translations.literal: " Yuanfu said: "Though they are numerous, their elite troops are very few—those who have drawn up their lines relying on the western hills are the ones; the rest need not be feared.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanfu said: "They are many but their crack troops are few—the men lined up along the western hills are the real threat; the rest we need not fear.

sentences.zh: 元福請以麾下騎先擊西山兵，公但嚴陣不動，俟敵少卻，當舉黃旗為號；

translations.literal: Yuanfu requested to lead the cavalry under his command to strike the western-hill troops first; "Your Lordship need only hold the battle line firm without moving; when the enemy begins to waver, raise a yellow flag as the signal;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu proposed to lead his cavalry in a first strike against the western-hill troops: "Your Lordship need only hold your formation steady; when the enemy begins to give ground, raise a yellow flag as the signal;

sentences.zh: 旗舉則合勢進擊，敗之必矣。

translations.literal: When the flag is raised, combine forces and advance to attack—they will surely be defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the flag goes up, combine forces and attack together—they cannot fail to be broken.

sentences.zh: 」暉然其策，遂率眾進擊，敵眾果潰。

translations.literal: " Hui approved of this plan and thereupon led the masses in an advance attack; the enemy forces indeed collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hui approved the plan and led his forces forward; the enemy ranks broke and fled as predicted.

sentences.zh: 元福即舉黃旗以招暉，暉軍繼進，彥超大敗，橫屍蔽野。

translations.literal: Yuanfu immediately raised the yellow flag to summon Hui; Hui's army followed in advance; Yanchao was utterly routed; corpses lay across the fields blocking the view.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu raised the yellow flag to signal Hui; Hui's army pressed forward and Yanchao was utterly routed, until corpses carpeted the plain.

sentences.zh: 是夕，入清邊軍。

translations.literal: That evening they entered Qingbian garrison.
translations.idiomatic: That evening they reached Qingbian garrison.

sentences.zh: 明日，至靈州。

translations.literal: The next day they reached Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they arrived at Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元福還郡，詔賜暉、元福衣帶繒帛銀器。

translations.literal: Yuanfu returned to his prefecture; an edict bestowed on Hui and Yuanfu robes, belts, silks, and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanfu returned to his command, an edict awarded Hui and Yuanfu robes, belts, silks, and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，從趙暉討王景崇於鳳翔。

translations.literal: During the Gan'you era of Han he followed Zhao Hui to campaign against Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Gan'you era of Later Han he followed Zhao Hui in the campaign against Wang Jingchong at Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 時兵力寡弱，不滿萬人，蜀兵數萬來援，景崇至寶雞，依山列柵。

translations.literal: At the time military strength was sparse and weak—fewer than ten thousand men; Shu troops numbering tens of thousands came to relieve them; Jingchong reached Baoji and drew up palisades along the hills.
translations.idiomatic: At the time their forces were weak, numbering fewer than ten thousand; tens of thousands of Shu troops came to Wang Jingchong's aid; Jingchong reached Baoji and erected palisades along the hills.

sentences.zh: 都監李彥從以數千人擊蜀軍，眾寡不敵，漢軍少卻。

translations.literal: Overseer Li Yancong with several thousand men attacked the Shu army; they were unequal to the great mass; the Han army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Overseer Li Yancong led several thousand men against the Shu forces but was outnumbered, and the Han army gave ground.

sentences.zh: 元福領數百騎自後驅之，下令還顧者斬，眾皆殊死戰，大敗蜀兵，追至大散關，殺三千餘人，餘皆棄甲遁去。

translations.literal: Yuanfu led several hundred cavalry and drove them from behind; he ordered that anyone who looked back would be beheaded; all fought to the death; the Shu army was utterly routed; they pursued to Dasan Pass, killed more than three thousand men, and the rest cast off their armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu led several hundred cavalry and drove the men forward from the rear, decreeing death for anyone who turned back; the soldiers fought as if their lives depended on it and routed the Shu army; the pursuit reached Dasan Pass, where more than three thousand were killed and the rest threw off their armor and fled.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔平，以功遷淄州刺史。

translations.literal: When Fengxiang was pacified, for his merit he was transferred to prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Fengxiang was pacified he was promoted to prefect of Zi Prefecture for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，王彥超討徐州叛將楊溫，以元福為行營兵馬都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun, Wang Yanchao campaigned against the rebel general of Xuzhou Yang Wen; Yuanfu was made horse-and-army overseer of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun, Wang Yanchao campaigned against Yang Wen, the rebel general of Xuzhou, with Yuanfu as horse-and-army overseer of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數月克之，率師還京，改陳州防禦使。

translations.literal: After several months it was taken; he led the army back to the capital and was transferred to defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell after several months; he led his army back to the capital and was appointed defense commissioner of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劉崇引契丹擾晉州，命樞密使王峻率兵拒之，以元福為西北面都排陣使。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Chong brought in the Khitan to harry Jin Prefecture; Grand Councilor Wang Jun was ordered to lead troops to resist; Yuanfu was made chief battle-array officer of the northwest sector.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Chong induced the Khitan to raid Jin Prefecture; Grand Councilor Wang Jun was ordered to oppose them, with Yuanfu as chief battle-array officer of the northwest sector.

sentences.zh: 軍過蒙坑，崇夜燒營遁。

translations.literal: When the army passed Mengkeng, Chong burned his camp by night and fled.
translations.idiomatic: As the army passed Mengkeng, Chong burned his camp and fled under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 峻令元福與仇超、陳思讓追至霍邑，既行，又遣止之。

translations.literal: Jun ordered Yuanfu together with Qiu Chao and Chen Siliang to pursue as far as Huoyi; after they had set out, he again sent orders to halt them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun ordered Yuanfu, Qiu Chao, and Chen Siliang to pursue as far as Huoyi, but after they had set out he sent orders to halt the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 元福謂思讓等曰：「劉崇召契丹擾邊，志在疲弊中國，今兵未交而遁，宜追奔深入，以挫其勢。

translations.literal: Yuanfu said to Siliang and the others: "Liu Chong summoned the Khitan to harry the border, intending to wear down the Central State; now, before battle has been joined, he has fled—we should pursue the fleeing enemy in depth to blunt his momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu said to Siliang and the others: "Liu Chong brought in the Khitan to harry our borders, aiming to exhaust the realm; he has fled before a blow has been struck—we should pursue him deep into enemy territory and break his momentum.

sentences.zh: 」諸將畏懦，遂止。

translations.literal: " The generals were timid and fearful, and so halted.
translations.idiomatic: " The other generals lost their nerve and called off the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 周祖知其事，明年，因調兵戍晉州，謂左右曰：「去年劉崇之遁，若從藥元福之言，則無邊患矣。」

translations.literal: The Zhou founder learned of this matter; the next year, when mobilizing troops to garrison Jin Prefecture, he said to those around him: "When Liu Chong fled last year, had we followed Yao Yuanfu's counsel, there would have been no border trouble."
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder learned of this, the following year, as he mobilized troops to garrison Jin Prefecture, he said to his attendants: "Had we heeded Yao Yuanfu's advice when Liu Chong fled last year, we would not face these border troubles now."

sentences.zh: 俄與曹英、向訓討慕容彥超於兗州，元福為行營馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Soon he campaigned with Cao Ying and Xiang Xun against Murong Yanchao at Yan Prefecture; Yuanfu served as chief adjutant of the horse and infantry armies of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Cao Ying and Xiang Xun in the campaign against Murong Yanchao at Yan Prefecture, serving as chief adjutant of the field headquarters horse and infantry armies.

sentences.zh: 詔元福自晉州率所部入朝，即遣東行，賜六銖、袍帶、鞍馬、器仗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yuanfu from Jin Prefecture to lead his command to court; he was immediately sent eastward and given a six-zhu weight ornament, robe and belt, saddle horse, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yuanfu to lead his command from Jin Prefecture to court; he was immediately sent east and given a six-zhu weight ornament, robe and belt, saddle horse, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 周祖謂曰：「比用曹州防禦使鄭璋，我度彥超兇狡，多計謀，恐璋不能集事，選爾代之。

translations.literal: The Zhou founder said to him: "Recently I employed Cao Prefecture defense commissioner Zheng Zhang; I reckoned Yanchao was fierce and cunning, full of stratagems, and feared Zhang could not accomplish the task—I chose you to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou founder told him: "I had appointed Zheng Zhang, defense commissioner of Cao Prefecture, to this command, but Yanchao is vicious and cunning and full of stratagems; I feared Zhang would not prevail, so I chose you to take his place.

sentences.zh: 已敕曹英、向訓不令以軍禮見汝。

translations.literal: I have already ordered Cao Ying and Xiang Xun not to receive you with military courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: I have already instructed Cao Ying and Xiang Xun not to treat you as a subordinate in military matters.

sentences.zh: 」及至軍中，英、訓皆尊禮之，當時有為宿將。

translations.literal: " When he reached the army, Ying and Xun both honored him with respect; at the time he counted as a veteran general.
translations.idiomatic: " When he joined the army, Ying and Xun both treated him with every mark of respect; he was regarded at the time as a veteran commander.

sentences.zh: 築連城以圍兗，彥超晝夜出兵，元福屢擊敗之，遂閉壁不敢出。

translations.literal: They built linked fortifications to besiege Yan; Yanchao sent troops out day and night; Yuanfu repeatedly defeated them, and Yanchao then shut his gates and dared not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: They built a chain of fortifications to besiege Yan Prefecture; Yanchao sent sorties day and night, but Yuanfu repulsed them again and again until Yanchao shut the gates and dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，元福營柵皆就，又穴地及築土山，百道攻其城。

translations.literal: After more than ten days, Yuanfu's camp palisades were all complete; they also dug tunnels and built earthen mounds, attacking the city from a hundred directions.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days, Yuanfu's camp fortifications were all in place. His men also dug tunnels and piled earthen mounds, then assailed the city from every side.

sentences.zh: 會周祖親征，元福以所部先入羊馬城，諸軍鼓噪角進，拔之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou came in person on campaign, Yuanfu led his own troops first into Yangma City; the armies beat drums, shouted, and blew horns as they advanced and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder arrived to take command in person, Yuanfu led his own troops in first at Yangma City. The armies raised a clamor of drums and horns as they pressed forward and captured the place.

sentences.zh: 以功授建雄軍節度。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed military governor of the Jianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was made military governor of the Jianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 世宗高平之戰，劉崇敗走太原，遂縱兵圍其城。

translations.literal: At Emperor Shizong's Battle of Gaoping, Liu Chong was defeated and fled to Taiyuan; the army was then unleashed to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Shizong's victory at Gaoping, Liu Chong was routed and fled back to Taiyuan, where the Zhou army pressed on and laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 以元福為同州節度，充太原四面壕砦都部署。

translations.literal: Yuanfu was made military governor of Tong Prefecture and appointed chief coordinator of trenches and fortifications on all four sides of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu was appointed military governor of Tong Prefecture and put in overall charge of the trenches and strongpoints surrounding Taiyuan on every side.

sentences.zh: 時攻具悉備，城中危急，以糧運不繼，詔令班師。

translations.literal: At the time the siege equipment was fully prepared and the city was in dire peril, but because grain transport could not keep up, an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: By then the siege equipment was complete and the city was in desperate straits, yet grain supplies could not be maintained, so the court ordered the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 元福上言曰：「進軍甚易，退軍甚難。

translations.literal: Yuanfu submitted a memorial saying, "Advancing the army is very easy; withdrawing the army is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfu memorialized the throne: "It is easy to advance, but far harder to retreat.

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「一以委卿。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong said, "I leave it entirely to you.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied, "I leave the whole matter in your hands.

sentences.zh: 」遂部分卒伍為方陣而南，元福以麾下為後殿，崇果出兵來追，元福擊走之。

translations.literal: " He then divided the troops into square formations and marched south; Yuanfu took his personal command as the rear guard. Chong indeed sent troops in pursuit, and Yuanfu struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: " The army was then formed into square battle arrays and marched south, with Yuanfu and his own troops serving as rear guard. Liu Chong did send forces in pursuit, but Yuanfu beat them back.

sentences.zh: 師還，加檢校太尉，移鎮陜州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant and transferred to command at Shaan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the army came home, he was given the honorary title of Grand Commandant and transferred to serve as prefectural commander at Shaan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又歷定、廬、曹三鎮。

translations.literal: He also successively held the three commands of Ding, Lu, and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: He later held successive commands at Ding, Lu, and Cao as well.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song dynasty, he was further promoted to honorary Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 九月卒，年七十七，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth month at the age of seventy-seven and was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month at the age of seventy-seven and was posthumously ennobled as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元福雖老，筋骨不衰，人或言其氣貌益壯，當復領兵，必大喜，曲致禮待，或加以贈遣，時稱驍將。

translations.literal: Although Yuanfu was old, his sinews and bones had not declined. When people said his bearing looked even more vigorous and that he would again lead troops, he would be greatly delighted; they would treat him with every courtesy and sometimes add gifts, and at the time he was called a fierce general.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years, Yuanfu remained physically vigorous. Whenever someone suggested that he looked stronger than ever and might take the field again, he would be overjoyed; people treated him with elaborate courtesy and often sent gifts, and he was widely regarded as a formidable commander.

sentences.zh: 趙晁，真定人。

translations.literal: Zhao Chao was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chao was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 初事杜重威為列校。

translations.literal: At first he served Du Chongwei as a company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Du Chongwei as a company commander.

sentences.zh: 重威誅，屬周祖鎮鄴中，晁因委質麾下。

translations.literal: When Chongwei was executed, Emperor Taizu of Zhou was stationed at Ye; Chao thereupon pledged allegiance under his command.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongwei was put to death, Chao offered his allegiance to the Zhou founder when the latter was stationed at Ye.

sentences.zh: 周祖開國，擢為作坊副使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou founded the state, Chao was promoted to deputy commissioner of the workshops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou dynasty was established, he was promoted to deputy commissioner of the imperial workshops.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超據兗州叛，以晁為行營步軍都監。

translations.literal: When Murong Yanchao held Yan Prefecture in rebellion, Chao was made superintendent of campaign infantry.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yanchao rebelled and seized Yan Prefecture, Chao was appointed superintendent of the campaign infantry.

sentences.zh: 兗州平，轉作坊使。

translations.literal: When Yan Prefecture was pacified, he was transferred to commissioner of the workshops.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan Prefecture was pacified, he was transferred to commissioner of the workshops.

sentences.zh: 晁自以逮事霸府，復有軍功，而遷拜不滿所望，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Chao considered that he had long served the hegemonic headquarters and again had military merit, yet his promotions and appointments fell short of his hopes, and he was habitually discontented.
translations.idiomatic: Chao felt that, having served the Zhou founder's headquarters from early on and earned military distinction besides, his promotions had not matched his expectations, and he was often sullen.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使王峻秉政，晁疑其軋己。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Councilor Wang Jun held power, and Chao suspected that Jun was suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun, the chief councilor of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was then in power, and Chao suspected that he was being deliberately sidelined.

sentences.zh: 一日使酒詣其第，毀峻，峻不之責。

translations.literal: One day, drunk, he went to Jun's residence and reviled him; Jun did not hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: One day, in his cups, he went to Jun's house and abused him to his face, yet Jun did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，改控鶴左廂都指揮使、領賀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, Chao was made commander of the left wing of the Controlled Cranes Guard and concurrently prefect of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, Chao was made commander of the left wing of the Controlled Cranes Guard and concurrently prefect of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從征劉崇，轉虎捷右廂都指揮使、領本州團練使兼行營步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: On campaign against Liu Chong, he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Fierce Tigers Guard, concurrently regimental commissioner of his home prefecture and commander of campaign infantry.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Liu Chong, he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Fierce Tigers Guard, made regimental commissioner of his home prefecture, and appointed commander of the campaign infantry.

sentences.zh: 軍至河內，世宗意在速戰，令晁倍道兼行。

translations.literal: When the army reached Henei, Emperor Shizong intended a swift battle and ordered Chao to march at double speed by forced stages.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Henei, Emperor Shizong wanted a quick decision and ordered Chao to force the march at top speed.

sentences.zh: 晁私語通事舍人鄭好謙曰：「賊勢方盛，未易敵也，宜持重以挫其銳。

translations.literal: Chao privately told the palace usher Zheng Haoqian, "The enemy's strength is at its height and is not easy to oppose; one should act with caution to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Chao took Zheng Haoqian, a palace usher, aside and said, "The enemy is at the height of his power and will not be easy to face. We ought to proceed cautiously and wear down his momentum.

sentences.zh: 」好謙以所言入白，世宗怒曰：「汝安得此言，必他人所教。

translations.literal: " Haoqian reported what had been said to the emperor. Emperor Shizong angrily said, "How dare you speak such words? Someone else must have taught you.
translations.idiomatic: " Haoqian repeated this to the emperor, who flew into a rage. "How dare you say such a thing? Someone must have put you up to it.

sentences.zh: 言其人，則舍爾；

translations.literal: Name that person and I will spare you;
translations.idiomatic: Name the man who said it, and I will spare you;

sentences.zh: 不言，當死！

translations.literal: if you do not speak, you shall die!
translations.idiomatic: if you refuse to speak, you die!

sentences.zh: 」好謙懼，遂以實對。

translations.literal: " Haoqian was afraid and thereupon answered with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: " Terrified, Haoqian told him the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 世宗即命並晁械於州獄，軍回始赦之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong immediately ordered Chao fettered as well and imprisoned in the prefectural jail; only when the army returned was he pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once had Chao shackled and thrown into the prefectural prison as well; he was not pardoned until the army returned.

sentences.zh: 及征淮南，改虎捷左廂、領閬州防禦使，充前軍行營步軍都指揮使，又為緣江步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the Huainan campaign was undertaken, he was transferred to the left wing of the Fierce Tigers Guard, made defense commissioner of Lang Prefecture, appointed commander of the vanguard campaign infantry, and also made commander of the riverine infantry.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Huainan, he was transferred to the left wing of the Fierce Tigers Guard, made defense commissioner of Lang Prefecture, and appointed commander of both the vanguard campaign infantry and the riverine infantry forces.

sentences.zh: 時李重進敗吳人於正陽，以降卒三千人付晁，晁一夕盡殺之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Chongjin defeated the Wu forces at Zhengyang and handed three thousand surrendered soldiers over to Chao; in one night Chao killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chongjin routed the Wu army at Zhengyang, he turned three thousand prisoners over to Chao, who had every one of them slaughtered in a single night.

sentences.zh: 世宗不之罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong did not punish him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 壽春平，拜檢校太保、河陽三城節度、孟懷等州觀察措置等使。

translations.literal: When Shouchun was pacified, he was appointed honorary Grand Guardian, military governor of the Heyang Three Cities, and commissioner for observation and disposition in Meng, Huai, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouchun fell, he was made honorary Grand Guardian, military governor of the Heyang Three Cities, and commissioner overseeing observation and administration in Meng, Huai, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Chao was promoted to honorary Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong came to the throne, he was further promoted to honorary Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 宋初，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song dynasty, he was promoted to honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以疾歸京師，卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: Before long, ill, he returned to the capital and died at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fell ill, returned to the capital, and died at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚悼之，贈太子太師，再贈侍中。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu deeply mourned him and posthumously granted him the title of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, then again granted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu mourned him deeply, posthumously ennobling him as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and later elevating the grant to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 晁身長七尺，儀貌雄偉，好聚斂，處方鎮以賄聞。

translations.literal: Chao was seven feet tall, with an imposing bearing, fond of amassing wealth, and while stationed in regional commands was known for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Chao stood seven feet tall, with a commanding presence. He was greedy for gain, and while serving in regional commands he became notorious for corruption.

sentences.zh: 以周初與宣祖分掌禁軍，有宗盟之分，故太祖常優禮之，再加贈典焉。

translations.literal: Because at the beginning of Zhou he and the Founding Ancestor had jointly commanded the forbidden army and shared the bond of sworn brotherhood, Emperor Taizu always treated him with special favor and again added to his posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhou years he and the Founding Ancestor had shared command of the palace army and stood in the relation of sworn brothers, so Emperor Taizu always treated him with exceptional courtesy and later added further posthumous honors as well.

sentences.zh: 子延溥。

translations.literal: His son was Yanbo.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yanbo.

sentences.zh: 子 延溥

translations.literal: Son: Yanbo
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yanbo

sentences.zh: 延溥，周顯德中，以父任補左班殿直。

translations.literal: Yanbo, in the Xiande era of Zhou, entered office through his father's position and was appointed a left-rank palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, during the Zhou Xiande era, received an appointment through his father's influence and was made a left-rank palace guard.

sentences.zh: 宋初，為鐵騎指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was made commander of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song dynasty, he was made commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 開寶初，太祖親征晉陽，太宗守京邑，延溥以所部為帳下牙軍，轉殿前散員指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaibao, when Emperor Taizu personally campaigned against Jinyang and Emperor Taizong guarded the capital, Yanbo took his own troops as the personal guard under the commander's banner and was transferred to commander of the Palace Front's miscellaneous guards.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaibao era, when Emperor Taizu marched in person against Jinyang and the future Emperor Taizong remained to guard the capital, Yanbo served with his own troops as a personal guard in the field headquarters and was then made commander of the Palace Front's miscellaneous guards.

sentences.zh: 九年，改鐵騎都虞候。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to deputy commander of the Iron Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made deputy commander of the Iron Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 五年，殿前白進超卒，即日以延溥為日騎、天武左右廂都指揮使，兼權殿前都虞候事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Bai Jinchao of the Palace Front died; that same day Yanbo was made commander of the left and right wings of the Sun Cavalry and Celestial Martial Guards and concurrently acted as deputy commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Bai Jinchao of the Palace Front died, and that same day Yanbo was appointed commander of the left and right wings of the Sun Cavalry and Celestial Martial Guards, with concurrent acting authority as deputy commander of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 坐遣親吏市竹木所過關渡稱制免算，責授登州團練使，令赴任。

translations.literal: Because he had sent a personal clerk to buy bamboo and timber and, at passes and ferry crossings along the way, claimed an imperial exemption from tolls, he was demoted and appointed regimental commissioner of Deng Prefecture and ordered to take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for sending a personal clerk to purchase bamboo and timber and having tolls waived at every pass and crossing by falsely claiming an imperial exemption; he was demoted to regimental commissioner of Deng Prefecture and ordered to take up his post at once.

sentences.zh: 是冬，帝北巡至大名，復以延溥為本州防禦使，即命為幽州東路行營壕砦都監。

translations.literal: That winter, when the emperor toured north as far as Daming, Yanbo was again made defense commissioner of that prefecture and immediately appointed superintendent of trenches and fortifications for the eastern-route campaign headquarters toward You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the emperor toured the north as far as Daming, Yanbo was restored as defense commissioner of that prefecture and at once appointed superintendent of trenches and fortifications for the eastern Youzhou campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 詔修緣邊城壘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the repair of frontier city ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered by edict to repair the fortified cities along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加涼州觀察使，仍判登州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was promoted to observation commissioner of Liang Prefecture while still serving concurrently as administrator of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was promoted to observation commissioner of Liang Prefecture while continuing to administer Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又為鎮州兵馬都部署，俄判霸州。

translations.literal: He was again made chief deployer of troops and horses at Zhen Prefecture, and soon thereafter concurrently administered Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made chief deployer of troops and horses at Zhen Prefecture, and shortly afterward was given concurrent charge of Ba Prefecture as well.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，改蔚州觀察使，判冀州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was transferred to observation commissioner of Yu Prefecture and administrator of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was made observation commissioner of Yu Prefecture and administrator of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會命曹彬等北征，又與內衣庫使張紹勍、引進副使董愿為幽州西北道行營都監。

translations.literal: When Cao Bin and others were ordered on the northern campaign, he was again appointed, together with the Inner Garment Store commissioner Zhang Shaoxing and the deputy usher Dong Yuan, superintendent of the northwest-route campaign headquarters toward You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Bin and others were sent on the northern expedition, he was again appointed, together with Zhang Shaoxing of the Inner Garment Store and Deputy Usher Dong Yuan, superintendent of the northwest Youzhou campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師還，命知貝州，改滑州部署。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was ordered to govern Bei Prefecture and transferred to deployer at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was appointed prefect of Bei Prefecture and then transferred to deployer at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，再知貝州，以疾求代，代未至，卒，年五十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again governed Bei Prefecture. Ill, he requested a replacement; before the replacement arrived, he died at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again served as prefect of Bei Prefecture. When illness forced him to request a successor, he died before the replacement arrived, at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 贈天德軍節度。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title of military governor of the Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as military governor of the Tiande Army.

sentences.zh: 子承彬，至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Chengbin rose to the rank of honored officer of the Inner Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengbin rose to the rank of honored officer of the Inner Hall.

sentences.zh: 承彬子咸一，為虞部員外郎，知宗正丞事。

translations.literal: Chengbin's son Xianyi served as an external secretary in the Ministry of Works and handled the affairs of the director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengbin's son Xianyi served as an external secretary in the Ministry of Works and handled the duties of the director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 咸熙，天聖八年進十及第。

translations.literal: Xianxi passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xianxi passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 論曰：侯益在晉、漢時，數為反覆，觀其受命契丹，私交偽蜀，赤岡之戰，復夜謁周祖，宗屬長幼，遭景崇鯨鯢，殆無噍類，推其心跡，豈懷貳之罰歟？

translations.literal: The commentators say: Hou Yi, during Jin and Han, repeatedly switched sides. Consider that he accepted orders from the Khitan, maintained private dealings with the false Shu, and at the Battle of Chigang again visited Emperor Taizu of Zhou by night; his clansmen, young and old, met Jing Chong's devastation and were nearly wiped out to the last survivor. Weighing his heart and his track record, was this not punishment for disloyalty?
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: During the Jin and Han dynasties, Hou Yi changed sides again and again. He accepted Khitan orders, maintained secret ties with the puppet Shu regime, and at the Battle of Chigang again went by night to pay court to the Zhou founder; his kinsmen, young and old, were engulfed by Liu Chong's fury until scarcely a soul survived. Judging by his conduct and its consequences, was this not the penalty for a treacherous heart?

sentences.zh: 薛懷讓、趙晁為將，皆忍於殺降。

translations.literal: Xue Huairang and Zhao Chao, as generals, were both ruthless in killing those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: As commanders, both Xue Huairang and Zhao Chao were merciless toward prisoners who had surrendered.

sentences.zh: 晁子延溥，能救後至之誅，雖父子之親，仁暴相戾有若是者。

translations.literal: Chao's son Yanbo was able to rescue men from execution for arriving late; though they were father and son, benevolence and cruelty could diverge to such a degree.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's son Yanbo, by contrast, could intercede to spare men condemned for tardiness; even between father and son, kindness and brutality could stand so far apart.

sentences.zh: 餘皆逢時奮武，致身榮顯。

translations.literal: The rest all seized the times to exert martial valor and attained honor and eminence.
translations.idiomatic: The others all seized their moment on the battlefield and rose to wealth and distinction.

sentences.zh: 扈彥珂請擊河中，卒用其策，愚者之一慮云。

translations.literal: Hu Yanke requested an attack on Hezhong, and in the end his plan was adopted—one bright thought from a foolish man, as it were.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yanke proposed an attack on Hezhong, and in the end his plan was adopted—a rare stroke of insight from an otherwise foolish man.
